subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which one of the following physical quantities has the same dimensions as that of Planck's constant (h)?
exp: Planck's constant has dimensions of energy × time = J·s = kg·m²·s⁻¹, which is the dimension of action and also of angular momentum (L = mvr). Linear momentum is kg·m·s⁻¹, force is kg·m·s⁻², and energy is kg·m²·s⁻² — all dimensionally different from h.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which one of the following statements is not correct?
options: The response of the ear to sound of increasing intensity is approximately logarithmic.
The sensitivity of the human ear does not vary with the frequency of the sound.
When two or more waves traverse the same medium, the displacement of any element is the algebraic sum of the displacements due to each wave.
Longitudinal waves can travel in all media — solids, liquids and gases.
exp: Ear sensitivity is strongly frequency-dependent — humans hear best around 2–5 kHz and poorly near 20 Hz or 20 kHz — so statement b is false. The logarithmic response (basis of the decibel scale), the principle of superposition, and the ability of longitudinal waves to travel through all material media are all correct.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The energy of a photon whose momentum is 10 MeV/c, where c is the speed of light, is
exp: For a photon (massless), energy and momentum are related by E = pc. With p = 10 MeV/c, E = (10 MeV/c)·c = 10 MeV. The other values would require a different momentum–energy relation, which does not apply to light.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: For which one of the following does the centre of mass lie outside the body?
exp: The centre of mass of a ring lies at its geometric centre — which is empty space, i.e. outside the material of the body. For a solid pen, ball or book the centre of mass falls within the material itself.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement regarding the jet stream is not correct?
options: It is a narrow band of high-velocity wind.
It follows a wavy path near the tropopause at elevations of 8–15 km.
Jet streams are typically continuous over long distances.
In summer, the polar front jet achieves its maximum force.
exp: The polar front jet stream is strongest in winter, when the temperature contrast between polar and tropical air is greatest; in summer it weakens and shifts poleward — so statement d is false. Jet streams are indeed narrow, fast, wavy bands of wind near the tropopause. (This is essentially a geography question.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statements are correct?
exp: LIGO's second confirmed detection (GW151226) was announced in June 2016 (1) and came from a black-hole merger (2). Gravitational waves come from merging compact objects (black holes/neutron stars), not white-dwarf collisions, so statement 3 is false.
subs: 1. In June 2016 the LIGO group announced detection of a second set of gravitational waves.
2. The waves were generated by the merger of two black holes about 1.4 billion light-years distant.
3. The waves were generated by collision of two white dwarf stars about 1.4 billion light-years distant.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: An electron and a proton starting from rest are accelerated through a potential difference of 1000 V. Which statement is correct?
options: The kinetic energy of both particles will be different.
The speed of the electron will be higher than that of the proton.
The speed of the proton will be higher than that of the electron.
exp: Both gain the same kinetic energy, KE = qV, since the magnitude of their charge is equal. But KE = ½mv², and the electron is ~1836 times lighter than the proton, so for equal KE the electron acquires a much higher speed.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: An object on a horizontal frictionless surface has gravity and the normal reaction acting on it, giving zero net force. What can be said about its motion (after being given a push)?
options: It moves with constant speed but varying direction.
exp: Gravity (down) and the normal force (up) cancel, so the net force is zero. By Newton's first law a body with no net force moves in a straight line at constant velocity (uniform speed and unchanging direction). (The question's reference to the third law is a misstatement — the balancing of gravity and normal force is not a third-law action-reaction pair.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Consider:
exp: In equilibrium the net torque (moment) is zero (1, correct). Momentum is conserved only when no external force acts, and kinetic energy is conserved only in elastic interactions — so the blanket claims in 2 and 3 are false. Hence only statement 1 holds.
subs: 1. There is no net moment on a body in equilibrium.
2. The momentum of a body is always conserved.
3. The kinetic energy of an object is always conserved. Which are correct?

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Consider the following statements:
options: Both true, II correctly explains I
Both true, II not the correct explanation of I
exp: Both statements are individually true, but the Earth's west-to-east rotation is not what causes tides — tides arise mainly from the Moon's (and Sun's) gravitational pull. So II is true but does not explain I.
subs: Statement I: Tides are caused by the combined gravitational forces of the Moon and Sun and the Earth's rotation.
Statement II: The Earth rotates from west to east.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The pressure of a fluid varies with depth as P = P₀ + ρgh, where ρ is the fluid density. This expression is associated with
exp: P = P₀ + ρgh is the hydrostatic pressure relation, which follows from Pascal's law — pressure in a static fluid increases linearly with depth and is transmitted equally in all directions. Bernoulli applies to moving fluids; Archimedes deals with buoyancy.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A particle moves from rest with uniform acceleration. The percentage increase in displacement during the sixth second compared to the fifth second is about
exp: Distance in the nth second (from rest) = a(2n−1)/2. Fifth second = 4.5a, sixth second = 5.5a. Increase = (5.5 − 4.5)/4.5 ≈ 22%.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The position vector of a particle is r = 7î + 2t²ĵ + 3t k̂. Then the instantaneous velocity and acceleration respectively lie
exp: Velocity v = dr/dt = 4t ĵ + 3 k̂ — it has only y and z components, so it lies in the yz-plane. Acceleration a = dv/dt = 4 ĵ — purely along the y-direction. (Reconstructed from the garbled source vector.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: For an ideal gas, which statement does not hold true?
options: The speed of all gas molecules is the same.
The kinetic energies of all gas molecules are not the same.
The potential energy of the gas molecules is zero.
There is no interactive force between the molecules.
exp: Gas molecules follow the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed distribution — they have a wide range of speeds, not a single common speed, so statement a is false. In an ideal gas there are no intermolecular forces (hence zero potential energy), and molecular kinetic energies do vary.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The Sasakawa Award of the United Nations is given for work in the field of
exp: The UN Sasakawa Award is the most prestigious international award recognising excellence in disaster risk reduction. (A current-affairs/awards item rather than physics.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A car undergoes uniform circular motion. Its acceleration is
exp: In uniform circular motion the speed is constant but the direction of velocity changes continuously, producing a centripetal acceleration. Its magnitude is constant but its direction keeps changing, so as a vector it is not constant (and not zero).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: If the linear momentum of a moving object is doubled by applying a force, its kinetic energy will
exp: Kinetic energy relates to momentum as KE = p²/2m. Doubling p multiplies p² by 4, so the kinetic energy becomes four times its original value.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: When rivers discharge their waters from all directions into a lake or depression, the pattern is known as
exp: In a centripetal drainage pattern, streams converge inward from all sides into a central basin, lake or depression. (Radial is the opposite — streams flowing outward from a dome; dendritic is tree-like; trellis is rectangular.) (A geography item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The direction of acceleration in uniform circular motion is along the
options: tangent to the circle at the point of observation
exp: The acceleration is centripetal, pointing toward the centre of the circle, which is always perpendicular to the (tangential) velocity. It is not along the direction of motion or the tangent.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A bus starting from rest with uniform acceleration attains 20 km/h in 10 minutes. Its acceleration is
exp: Acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time = 20 km/h ÷ (10/60 h) = 20 ÷ 0.1667 = 120 km/h².

subject: Science & Technology
stem: An object weighs 9 N on Earth. Its weight on a planet where g is 9 times that of Earth would be
exp: Weight = mg. The mass is unchanged, but if g becomes 9 times larger, the weight becomes 9 × 9 = 81 N — i.e. nine times the Earth value.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The twinkling of a star is due to
options: continuous change in the position of the star
exp: Twinkling (stellar scintillation) occurs because starlight passes through atmospheric layers of varying density and refractive index, which continuously bend (refract) the light, making the star's apparent brightness and position fluctuate.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Match vaccine with type:
exp: Covaxin is an inactivated-virus vaccine (1, correct) and Sputnik V is a viral-vector vaccine (3, correct). Covishield is not an mRNA vaccine — it is a viral-vector (adenovirus) vaccine — so pair 2 is wrong. (The mRNA vaccines were Pfizer and Moderna.)
subs: 1. Covaxin – Inactivated pathogen-based
2. Covishield – mRNA vaccine
3. Sputnik V – Viral vector-based. Which pairs are correctly matched?

subject: Science & Technology
stem: An object of mass 10 kg moves at uniform speed 10 m/s. Its linear momentum and kinetic energy respectively are
exp: Momentum p = mv = 10 × 10 = 100 N·s; kinetic energy = ½mv² = ½ × 10 × 100 = 500 J.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: An object is dropped from a height onto the floor. Which quantity remains uniform as it falls?
exp: During free fall only gravity acts, so the acceleration stays constant at g (≈9.8 m/s²). Speed increases, so momentum and kinetic energy rise, while potential energy falls — only the acceleration is uniform.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The acceleration due to gravity at the Earth's surface depends on
options: either its mass or its radius
exp: Surface gravity is g = GM/R², so it depends on both the planet's mass M (directly) and its radius R (inversely as the square).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The area under the velocity–time graph for a particle moving in a straight line with uniform acceleration gives
exp: The area under a velocity–time graph equals displacement (velocity × time). For motion in one direction this also equals distance, but in general the signed area gives net displacement.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A charged particle moves through a magnetic field B with velocity v. The force F is
options: maximum when v and B are parallel
maximum when v and B are anti-parallel
maximum when v and B are perpendicular
independent of the angle between v and B
exp: The magnetic force is F = qvB sinθ. It is maximum when θ = 90° (v ⟂ B, sinθ = 1) and zero when v is parallel or anti-parallel to B (sinθ = 0).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: About the Race to Zero Campaign:
exp: The Race to Zero is a global UN-backed campaign to mobilise net-zero/decarbonization commitments (1, correct). It has nothing to do with the game-theory "zero-sum game" concept, so statement 2 is wrong.
subs: 1. A main objective is to build momentum around the shift to a decarbonized economy.
2. It is related to the theory of Zero-Sum Game.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which correctly describes the working principle of an atomic clock?
options: Vibration of a small quartz crystal
Simple harmonic motion of atoms inside a crystal
Resonant frequency in cesium or rubidium atom
Excitation and de-excitation of hydrogen atoms
exp: Atomic clocks keep time using the extremely stable resonant (hyperfine transition) frequency of atoms such as caesium or rubidium — the SI second is defined by 9,192,631,770 cycles of a caesium-133 transition. Quartz vibration is used in ordinary watches, not atomic clocks.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Identify the drainage pattern: most common; uniform rock type and regular slope; map looks like veins on a leaf with smaller streams joining the main stream at an acute angle.
exp: A dendritic pattern is the commonest, developing on uniform rock and gentle regular slopes; its tree/leaf-vein branching with tributaries meeting at acute angles is its signature. (A geography item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: 1. Angular velocity is the same for all locations on Earth's surface while linear velocity varies.
exp: Every point on Earth completes one rotation in 24 hours, so angular velocity is identical everywhere (1, correct). Linear (tangential) speed = ωr depends on distance from the axis, which is largest at the equator and zero at the poles (2, correct).
subs: 2. Linear velocity is maximum at the equator and minimum at the poles.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A motorcycle has initial velocity 5 m/s; after 3 s its velocity is 7 m/s. Its displacement in 3 s is
exp: For uniform acceleration, displacement = average velocity × time = [(5 + 7)/2] × 3 = 6 × 3 = 18 m.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement is not correct?
options: All bodies attract each other due to gravitational force.
Newton's law of gravitation follows from Newton's laws of motion.
The value of g at the centre of the Earth is zero.
Mass and weight are measured in different units.
exp: Newton's law of gravitation is an independent law, not derived from his three laws of motion — so statement b is false. Universal attraction, g = 0 at Earth's centre, and mass (kg) versus weight (newton) being different units are all correct.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The linear momentum of a particle is conserved if
options: the net force on it is maximum
the net force on it is zero
the net torque on it is zero
the net work done on it is maximum
exp: From Newton's second law, F = dp/dt, so momentum stays constant only when the net external force is zero. Torque governs angular momentum, and work relates to kinetic energy — neither conserves linear momentum.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: When a stone tied to a string is whirled in a circle, the work done on it by the string is
options: depends on the mass of the stone
exp: The string's tension provides the centripetal force, which points toward the centre — perpendicular to the stone's motion. Since work = F·d·cos90° = 0, the string does no work on the stone.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The reaction K₂SO₄(aq) + BaCl₂(aq) → 2KCl(aq) + BaSO₄(s) is an example of
exp: Two compounds exchange their ions (K⁺ pairs with Cl⁻, Ba²⁺ with SO₄²⁻), and an insoluble precipitate (BaSO₄) forms — the defining feature of a double displacement (precipitation) reaction. (Chemistry item placed in Mechanics by the source.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is the most characteristic property of an element?
exp: An element's identity is fixed by its atomic number (number of protons) — this never changes for a given element. Density and boiling point vary with conditions, and the mass number differs between isotopes of the same element.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Tuvalu has been in discussion recently. Why?
options: A potato plant that grows at high altitude
A place in equatorial Africa where snow is found
New technology to meet global warming
A country under threat of submergence due to ice melting and sea-level rise
exp: Tuvalu, a low-lying Pacific island nation, is among the countries most threatened by rising sea levels caused by climate change, risking submergence. (A climate/current-affairs item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The correct relation between Kelvin temperature T and Celsius temperature t is
exp: The Kelvin and Celsius scales have the same size of degree but a shifted zero — 0 °C = 273.15 K — so T = t + 273.15.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which represents the relation "heat lost = heat gained"?
exp: The principle of calorimetry states that, in an isolated system, the heat lost by the hot body equals the heat gained by the cold body until thermal equilibrium is reached. This is the basis of all heat-exchange (mixing) calculations.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not a primary function of a green leaf?
exp: Leaves carry out photosynthesis (food-making), gas exchange and transpiration (water evaporation). Conduction/transport of food and water is the job of the vascular tissues (xylem and phloem in the stem), not a primary leaf function. (A biology item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: In which case is heat loss primarily not due to convection?
options: Circulation of air around a blast furnace
Heating of the glass surface of a bulb due to current in the filament
exp: A bulb's glass is heated mainly by radiation (and conduction) from the glowing filament, not by convection. Boiling water, land/sea breezes and air circulation around a furnace are all classic convection processes.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: About mixtures:
exp: A pure substance cannot be split into other kinds of matter by physical means (only mixtures can), so statement 1 is wrong. Dissolved salt can be recovered from water by evaporation, a physical process (2, correct).
subs: 1. A substance can be separated into other kinds of matter by any physical process.
2. Dissolved sodium chloride can be separated from water by the physical process of evaporation.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: If x is the temperature in Kelvin and y in °C, the correct relation is
exp: Kelvin = Celsius + 273 (using the rounded value), so x = 273 + y.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Xylem conducts water upward. Which xylem tissue consists of living cells?
exp: Among xylem components, only xylem parenchyma is living; tracheids, vessels and fibres are dead, lignified cells at maturity. Parenchyma stores food and helps in short-distance transport. (A biology item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Identify the cloud: born through convection; only type producing hail, thunder and lightning; large cauliflower-shaped towers, often with anvil tops.
exp: Cumulonimbus are towering convective storm clouds with anvil tops, the only clouds that produce hail, thunder and lightning. (A geography/meteorology item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The correct relation between Celsius and Fahrenheit scales is
exp: The conversion is F = (9/5)C + 32. Note the source prints two identical correct options (c and d); the intended single correct expression is T_F = (9/5)T_C + 32.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A new concrete surface is covered with wet straw/gunny bags. This is done to
options: prevent fast evaporation until hydration has proceeded well
exp: This is curing of concrete. Keeping the surface moist slows water loss by evaporation so that the cement's hydration reactions can proceed fully, giving the concrete its strength.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which heat transfer is an example of convection?
options: Heating food in a microwave oven
Boiling water in a pot on a gas stove
Heating a brass rod at one end and feeling the rise at the other
exp: In boiling water, heated water rises and cooler water sinks, setting up convection currents — the bulk movement of fluid carrying heat. Microwave heating and sunlight are radiation, and heat moving along a brass rod is conduction.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Light travels in a straight line (rectilinear propagation). This holds if the medium is
options: made up of slabs of different refractive indices
exp: Light travels straight only when the medium has a uniform (homogeneous) refractive index; any change in refractive index bends the ray. A transparent, homogeneous medium offers no such variation, so light goes straight.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: An X-ray photon has 1 keV energy, a visible photon 3 eV. Which statement is not correct?
options: The X-ray wavelength is less than the visible wavelength.
The two photons have different energies.
The speeds of both photons in vacuum are different.
The X-ray frequency is higher than the visible frequency.
exp: All electromagnetic radiation travels at the same speed c in vacuum, regardless of energy or frequency — so statement c is false. The higher-energy X-ray correctly has a shorter wavelength and higher frequency.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The optical phenomenon primarily responsible for a rainbow is
exp: A rainbow forms when sunlight entering raindrops is dispersed — different colours refract by different amounts (and undergo internal reflection), splitting white light into the spectrum.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A ray strikes a plane mirror at 40° to the surface normal. On reflection it is deviated by
exp: The deviation produced by a plane mirror is 180° − 2i, where i is the angle of incidence. With i = 40°, deviation = 180° − 80° = 100°.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Regarding infrared, visible and ultraviolet radiation, which statement is not correct?
options: IR wavelength is more than UV wavelength.
UV wavelength is smaller than visible.
Photon energy of visible light is more than IR.
Photon energy of UV is lesser than that of visible light.
exp: Energy rises as wavelength shortens (E = hc/λ). UV has a shorter wavelength than visible light, so its photon energy is greater, not lesser — statement d is false. The other comparisons are correct.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which type of glass is used for making optical instruments?
exp: Flint glass, with its high refractive index and dispersion, is used for lenses and prisms in optical instruments. Pyrex is heat-resistant borosilicate glassware; soft/hard glasses are for general use.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Consider the following statements:
options: Both true, II not the explanation
exp: UV radiation does cause skin cancer (I true). But the stratospheric ozone layer absorbs/blocks most harmful UV rather than allowing it in — so Statement II is false.
subs: Statement I: Skin cancer is generally caused by ultraviolet radiation.
Statement II: The stratosphere allows ultraviolet radiation to enter the Earth from the Sun.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: When the Sun is near the horizon it appears reddish. The responsible phenomenon is
exp: Near the horizon, sunlight travels a long path through the atmosphere; shorter (blue) wavelengths are scattered away (Rayleigh scattering), leaving the transmitted light dominated by red, so the Sun looks reddish.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The visible portion of the electromagnetic spectrum is
exp: Visible light (about 400–700 nm) is the only part of the EM spectrum the human eye can detect. Infrared, microwave and radio waves are all invisible.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: When a convex lens produces a real image, the minimum distance between object and image equals
exp: The object–image separation is minimum when the object is at 2f (image also at 2f), giving a total of 4f. For any other position the separation is larger.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: If λ_UV, λ_visible and λ_IR are the wavelengths of ultraviolet, visible and infrared radiation, the correct relationship is
exp: Wavelength increases in the order UV (shortest) → visible → infrared (longest), so λ_UV < λ_visible < λ_IR. (Subscripts were garbled in the source and are reconstructed here.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The correct sequence of passage of light in a compound microscope is
exp: Light from the source is concentrated by the condenser, passes through the specimen into the objective lens, travels up the body tube, and finally reaches the eye through the eyepiece.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not a property of X-rays?
options: They are deflected by electric fields.
They are not deflected by magnetic fields.
They have high penetrating power in matter.
Their wavelength is much smaller than that of visible light.
exp: X-rays are electromagnetic waves with no charge, so they are not deflected by electric (or magnetic) fields — statement a is false. Their high penetration and very short wavelength are correct.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not true about the image formed by a plane mirror?
options: It is the same size as the object.
It is formed as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.
exp: A plane mirror always forms a virtual image (it cannot be caught on a screen), so statement c is false. The image is the same size, laterally inverted, and equidistant behind the mirror — all correct.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: If the speed of light in air is 3 × 10⁸ m/s, the speed in a medium of refractive index µ is
exp: Refractive index µ = c/v, so the speed in the medium is v = c/µ = (3 × 10⁸)/µ m/s. The printed options are corrupted; the physically correct value is c/µ.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which type of radiation has the shortest wavelength?
exp: Of the four, ultraviolet has the shortest wavelength (highest frequency/energy). The order from longest to shortest is radio > infrared > visible > ultraviolet.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The electromagnetic waves used for satellite communication are
exp: Satellite communication uses radio waves (specifically microwave-band radio), which pass through the atmosphere and ionosphere with little absorption — unlike visible, IR or UV light.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which one is not a coral reef island?
exp: Kyushu is a large volcanic/continental island of Japan, not a coral reef. The Great Barrier Reef, Fiji's Rainbow Reef and Swaraj Dweep (Havelock, Andamans) are all coral-reef environments. (A geography item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Regarding ultraviolet light, which statement is not correct?
options: Its wavelength is shorter than that of visible light.
exp: UV light, like all electromagnetic radiation, is a transverse wave, not longitudinal — so statement c is false. It does travel through vacuum and has a shorter wavelength than visible light.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: If c is the speed of light in air and v in a medium, the refractive index is
exp: Refractive index is defined as µ = c/v, the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum/air to its speed in the medium. Since v < c, µ is always greater than 1.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which lens bends light rays through the largest angle?
exp: The bending power is greater for larger magnitude of dioptric power (and shorter focal length). |2.5 D| is the largest, so this lens bends light most strongly.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: An object is placed 40 cm from a converging lens of focal length 25 cm. The image is
exp: The object lies between f (25 cm) and 2f (50 cm), so a convex lens forms a real, inverted, magnified image beyond 2f on the other side. (Calculation gives v ≈ 66.7 cm, magnification ≈ 1.7.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: When light enters glass from water at an angle of incidence of 0°, the angle of refraction is
options: the ray will not enter at all
exp: At normal incidence (0°) the ray travels along the normal and passes straight through without bending, so the angle of refraction is also 0°.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The Andaman & Nicobar islands were connected to the mainland by a Submarine Optical Fibre Cable. Which island was not connected initially?
exp: The 2020 OFC project linked Port Blair (the hub) with islands including Swaraj Dweep (Havelock), Little Andaman, Car Nicobar, Kamorta, Great Nicobar, Long Island and Rangat. Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island) was not among the initially connected nodes.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A non-spherical shining spoon can generally be considered as a
exp: The curved reflecting bowl of a spoon approximates a parabolic mirror — its concave (inner) and convex (outer) surfaces both behave like curved mirrors with a roughly parabolic profile, not a flat or perfectly spherical one.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: How many internal reflections of light occur in the formation of a primary rainbow?
exp: A primary rainbow forms by refraction–one internal reflection–refraction within each raindrop. (A secondary rainbow involves two internal reflections.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Where should an object be placed before a convex lens to get a real and enlarged image?
options: Between the principal focus and twice the focal length
exp: With the object between F and 2F, a convex lens forms a real, inverted, magnified (enlarged) image beyond 2F. At 2F the image is the same size; beyond 2F it is diminished.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Refraction of light, as it enters from one transparent medium to another, is due to
options: change in temperature of the media
exp: Light changes speed when it crosses into a medium of different refractive index, and this change in speed bends the ray — that is refraction.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: If the magnification produced by a lens is 2, the image is
exp: A magnification of +2 has a positive sign, so the image is erect and virtual, and the value 2 means it is larger than the object. Hence the image is erect, virtual and larger (option c).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement about a greenhouse is true?
options: Shorter-wavelength IR from the Sun can enter the greenhouse while longer-wavelength IR from inside cannot pass back out through the glass.
Shorter cannot enter while longer can pass out.
No IR can pass through the glass.
exp: Glass transmits the shorter-wavelength (near) infrared and visible sunlight in, but the ground and plants re-radiate longer-wavelength (far) infrared, which the glass traps — warming the interior. This is the greenhouse effect.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A convex lens has focal length 15 cm. At what object distance is a real image of the same size formed?
exp: A same-size real image forms when the object is at 2f = 2 × 15 = 30 cm; the image then also lies at 2f on the other side, with magnification 1.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: India recently commissioned its first liquid mirror telescope at
exp: The International Liquid Mirror Telescope was commissioned at Devasthal, Nainital, Uttarakhand — Asia's first, using a rotating dish of liquid mercury as the primary mirror.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A patient's abdomen can be examined by X-ray after administering which metal salt in the meal?
exp: Barium sulphate is an X-ray contrast agent (a "barium meal"): it is opaque to X-rays yet insoluble and non-toxic, so it coats the gut and reveals its outline. Soluble barium salts like barium chloride are poisonous.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: If an object is placed at the focus of a convex lens, its image is
options: at the focus on the same side
at the focus on the opposite side
exp: Rays from an object at the focus emerge parallel after passing through a convex lens, so the image is formed at infinity (highly magnified).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement about the aperture of a convex lens is correct?
options: It equals its radius of curvature.
It is independent of its radius of curvature.
It equals half its focal length.
exp: The aperture is the effective diameter through which light passes — a geometric property of lens size, unrelated to the focal length or radius of curvature (which depend on the surface curvature and refractive index).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The power of a lens of focal length 10 cm is
exp: Power P = 1/f (in metres). f = 10 cm = 0.1 m, so P = 1/0.1 = 10 dioptres.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A person can see near objects clearly but not distant ones (myopia). Possible reasons:
exp: Myopia (short-sightedness) results when the image forms in front of the retina — caused by an over-curved (too powerful) lens (1) or an elongated eyeball (4). A too-large focal length would make the eye under-powered (hypermetropia), so that reason is wrong.
subs: 1. Excessive curvature of the eye lens.
3. The focal length of the eye lens is too large.
4. Elongation of the eyeball.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: If the Moon is brought closer so its distance from Earth becomes half, the gravitational force of attraction would
exp: Gravitational force follows an inverse-square law, F ∝ 1/r². Halving the distance multiplies the force by 1/(½)² = 4.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A concave mirror of radius of curvature 50 cm forms an image of an object kept 25 cm from it. The image position is
exp: Focal length f = R/2 = 25 cm. The object is placed at the focus, so the reflected rays are parallel and the image forms at infinity.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which pair of event and year is not correctly matched?
options: Launch of the first communications satellite – 1962
Completion of a continuous round-the-world fibre-optic cable link – 1997
Introduction of the World Wide Web (www) – 1995
exp: The World Wide Web was invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989–1991, not 1995 — so this pairing is wrong. Telstar (first comms satellite) launched in 1962 and SWIFT was set up in 1973–77, which match acceptably.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: About Madurai, capital of the Pandya kingdom:
exp: All three descriptions of Madurai are supported by the textual sources cited (Maduraikkanchi, Arthashastra references to fine cotton, and craft-centre accounts). (This is a history question included under the science compilation.)
subs: 1. Described in Maduraikkanchi as a grand walled city with the Vaigai river on the fourth side.
2. The Arthashastra mentions it as a centre of fine cotton textiles.
3. Other sources describe it as a major craft centre.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: About Sawai Jai Singh's astronomical work:
exp: Sawai Jai Singh II drew on European astronomical observations and de La Hire's tables, so statement 1 is correct. The claim that his astronomers built their own telescope to observe Venus is not supported - hence 1 only.
subs: 1. He learnt of European observations and obtained de La Hire's tables, reproducing a refraction table.
2. His astronomers developed a telescope of their own to observe the lunar phases of Venus.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The formation of a rainbow by water droplets involves
options: both refraction and internal reflection of sunlight
exp: A rainbow forms by refraction (entry), internal reflection inside the drop, and refraction again (exit), accompanied by dispersion. So both refraction and internal reflection are involved.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: If your image appears erect no matter how far you stand from a mirror, the mirror is likely
exp: Plane and convex mirrors always form erect (virtual) images for any object distance. A concave mirror gives an inverted image when the object is beyond its focus, so it is excluded.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is used in a simple microscope?
exp: A simple microscope (magnifying glass) is a single convex (converging) lens that forms a magnified, erect, virtual image when the object is within its focal length.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: An X-ray can be deflected
options: by both electric and magnetic fields
neither by electric field nor by magnetic field
exp: X-rays are uncharged electromagnetic waves, so they are unaffected by electric or magnetic fields (unlike charged particles such as electrons).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: In a simple astronomical telescope, the objective and the eyepiece respectively are
options: a convergent lens and a divergent lens
a divergent lens and a divergent lens
a divergent lens and a convergent lens
a convergent lens and a convergent lens
exp: A refracting astronomical telescope uses two convex (convergent) lenses — a long-focal-length objective and a short-focal-length eyepiece.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Twinkling of a star is due to
exp: Starlight passing through atmospheric layers of changing density undergoes continuous atmospheric refraction, causing the apparent brightness/position to flicker — i.e. twinkling.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: In a bipolar junction transistor
options: all three regions have equal impurity concentrations
the emitter has the least concentration
the collector has the least concentration
the base has the least concentration of impurity
exp: In a BJT the base is lightly doped and very thin, the emitter is heavily doped, and the collector is moderately doped. The light base doping ensures most charge carriers from the emitter pass through to the collector.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Liquids and gases never show
exp: Ferromagnetism requires an ordered crystalline arrangement of magnetic domains, found only in certain solids (iron, cobalt, nickel). Liquids and gases lack this rigid domain structure, so they can be dia- or paramagnetic but never ferromagnetic.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: When pure silicon is doped with aluminium,
exp: Aluminium is trivalent (group 13); adding it to silicon creates holes (electron deficiencies), making the majority carriers positive — a p-type semiconductor. A pentavalent dopant would instead give n-type.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Voltage V across resistance R dissipates power P. The same V is applied across three equal resistors (each R) in parallel. The power dissipated is
exp: Three equal resistors R in parallel give an equivalent resistance R/3. Power = V²/R_eq = V²/(R/3) = 3V²/R = 3P.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not a semiconductor?
exp: Quartz (silicon dioxide) is an insulator (and a piezoelectric crystal). Silicon, germanium and gallium arsenide are all classic semiconductors.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A parallel-plate capacitor (air) has capacitance C. Filling the gap with a dielectric of constant 7 makes the capacitance
exp: Inserting a dielectric multiplies capacitance by the dielectric constant: C′ = κC = 7C.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Of wavelengths 200 nm, 500 nm and 1000 nm, which can produce a visual sensation in the human eye?
exp: The visible range is roughly 400–700 nm, so only 500 nm lies within it. 200 nm is ultraviolet and 1000 nm is infrared — both invisible.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: One parallel-plate capacitor uses gold plates, another uses aluminium plates, with the same separation and plate area. With ρg and ρa the resistivities of gold and aluminium, which relation is correct?
exp: Capacitance depends only on plate area, separation and the dielectric (here air) — not on the plate material or its resistivity. Same geometry therefore gives equal capacitance.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Two wires of equal length l and area A: wire 1 copper, wire 2 aluminium; copper has higher conductivity. Which is correct?
options: Equal current gives equal power dissipation
exp: Resistance R = l/(σA). Aluminium has lower conductivity σ, so for identical dimensions the aluminium wire (2) has higher resistance than the copper wire (1).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which political party was launched by Irom Sharmila in Manipur?
exp: Activist Irom Sharmila founded the People's Resurgence and Justice Alliance (PRJA) in 2016 to contest Manipur elections. (A polity/current-affairs item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Ultrasonic waves are produced by using
exp: Applying an alternating voltage to a piezoelectric crystal makes it vibrate at very high (ultrasonic) frequencies — the piezoelectric effect is the standard way to generate ultrasound.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Why is argon gas used along with tungsten wire in an electric bulb?
options: To increase the life of the bulb
exp: Argon is an inert gas that prevents the hot tungsten filament from oxidising and slows its evaporation, so the filament lasts longer.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Two copper wires of equal length; the radius of wire 1 is half that of wire
exp: Wire 2 has twice the radius, hence 4× the area and resistance R/4. In series, total = R + R/4 = 5R/4.
subs: 2. Wire 1 has resistance R. Joined in series, the total resistance is

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which does not convert electrical energy into light energy?
exp: A candle converts chemical energy into light (and heat), not electrical energy. LEDs, lasers and TVs all turn electrical energy into light.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A circuit has a 5 A fuse. The maximum number of 100 W, 220 V bulbs that can be safely connected in parallel is
exp: Each bulb draws I = P/V = 100/220 ≈ 0.45 A. The number that keeps total current ≤ 5 A is 5/0.45 ≈ 11 bulbs.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A 100 W bulb is used 10 hours a day. Units of energy consumed in 30 days?
exp: Energy = power × time = 0.1 kW × 10 h × 30 = 30 kWh = 30 units.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: If the speed of a magnet moving inside a coil increases, the induced current in the coil
exp: By Faraday's law, faster motion means a greater rate of change of magnetic flux, which induces a larger EMF and current.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Who is a pioneer in discovering the heating effect of electric current?
exp: James Prescott Joule established that heat produced in a conductor is proportional to I²Rt — Joule's law of heating.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which law of electromagnetism does not give the direction of the magnetic field?
exp: Faraday's law gives the magnitude of the induced EMF, not a direction (direction comes from Lenz's law). The right-hand thumb rule and Fleming's rules are specifically about directions.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: In a circuit with a cell, ammeter and nichrome wire, if the wire length is reduced to half, the ammeter reading
exp: Resistance is proportional to length, so halving the wire halves the resistance; by Ohm's law (I = V/R) the current doubles.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A bulb on a 110 V supply draws 0.2 A. Its power is
exp: Power P = VI = 110 × 0.2 = 22 W.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: At the time of a short circuit, the current in the circuit
exp: A short circuit provides a near-zero-resistance path, so by I = V/R the current rises sharply — which is why fuses/breakers trip to prevent fire.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement is not correct?
options: An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy.
A generator works on electromagnetic induction.
The magnetic field at the centre of a long current-carrying coil is parallel straight lines.
A wire with green insulation is usually the live wire.
exp: Green (or green-yellow) insulation denotes the earth/ground wire, not the live wire — so statement d is false. The motor, generator and solenoid-field statements are correct.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement about genetically modified organisms is not correct?
options: A gene from one organism is isolated and transferred to another.
This technique has applications only in plants.
Insect-resistance genes may spread from crops to wild plants.
Transgenic animals are made by inserting novel genes at a very early developmental stage.
exp: Genetic modification is applied to animals and microorganisms too (e.g. transgenic mice, GM bacteria producing insulin), not only plants — so statement b is false. (A biology item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: In a circuit with 10 µF capacitor, two 10 Ω resistors and a 10 V source, the steady current flowing is
exp: In the steady state a fully charged capacitor carries no current, so its branch is effectively open. The current flows through the two 10 Ω resistors (20 Ω): I = 10/20 = 0.5 A.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The device used to measure electric current in a circuit is the
exp: An ammeter (connected in series) measures current; a voltmeter measures potential difference, while motors and generators are energy-conversion devices.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A metal wire of length l and diameter d has resistance R. Another wire of the same metal and length but double the diameter has resistance
exp: Doubling the diameter gives 4× the cross-sectional area, and R ∝ 1/A, so the resistance falls to R/4.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A 100 W bulb used 10 hours a day. Units of electrical energy consumed in 3 days (1 unit = 1 kWh)?
exp: Energy = 0.1 kW × 10 h × 3 days = 3 kWh = 3.00 units.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Three resistors of 11 Ω, 22 Ω and 33 Ω are in parallel. Their equivalent resistance is
exp: 1/R = 1/11 + 1/22 + 1/33 = (6 + 3 + 2)/66 = 11/66 = 1/6, so R = 6 Ω. (Parallel resistance is always less than the smallest resistor.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not a ferromagnetic material?
exp: Silver is diamagnetic, not ferromagnetic. Iron and cobalt are the classic ferromagnets (ferric chloride contains ferromagnetic-element iron and is included as the intended distractor, but silver is the clear non-ferromagnetic metal).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A Van de Graaff generator generates
exp: A Van de Graaff generator accumulates static charge on a metal dome to build up very high DC potentials (millions of volts) at low current — used to accelerate charged particles.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not a property of graphene?
options: It is the thinnest material known.
It is a wide band-gap semiconductor.
exp: Graphene is a zero-band-gap semimetal (or "semiconductor with no band gap"), not a wide-band-gap semiconductor — so statement d is false. It is indeed atomically thin, nearly transparent, and an excellent conductor.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Sound waves cannot travel through
options: a copper wire placed in air
a silver slab placed in air
a glass prism placed in water
a wooden hollow pipe placed in vacuum
exp: Sound is a mechanical wave that needs a material medium; it cannot travel through vacuum. The hollow pipe in vacuum has no medium inside to carry the sound. The other options all have a solid/liquid medium.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: An echo is heard 5 s after a sound is made; sound speed is 340 m/s. The distance of the reflecting mountain is
exp: The sound travels to the mountain and back, so distance = (speed × time)/2 = (340 × 5)/2 = 850 m = 0.85 km.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A note one octave higher than 500 Hz has a frequency of
exp: Raising a note by one octave doubles its frequency, so 500 Hz → 1000 Hz.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The property of a sound wave that determines pitch is its
exp: Pitch is the perception of how high or low a sound is, governed by its frequency — higher frequency means higher pitch. Amplitude/intensity determine loudness.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A sound wave of frequency 4 kHz and wavelength 30 cm takes how long to travel 2.4 km?
exp: Speed = fλ = 4000 × 0.3 = 1200 m/s. Time = distance/speed = 2400/1200 = 2.0 s.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement about LOFAR (Low Frequency Array) is correct?
options: It is the world's most powerful radio antenna (telescope).
A NASA space technology to discover exoplanets.
An arrangement of satellites for a navigation system.
exp: LOFAR is a vast network of radio antennas (centred in the Netherlands) forming one of the world's most powerful low-frequency radio telescopes, used to study the early universe and cosmic radio sources.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The pitch of a sound wave depends on which characteristic?
exp: Pitch is determined by frequency — the higher the frequency, the higher the pitch. Amplitude relates to loudness, not pitch.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A firecracker burst before a cliff returns an echo 5 s later; sound speed 340 m/s. The cliff distance is close to
exp: Distance = (speed × time)/2 = (340 × 5)/2 = 850 m (the sound travels to the cliff and back in 5 s).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A sonic boom is produced when a source of sound travels at a speed
options: greater than the speed of sound
greater than the speed of light
lesser than the speed of sound
equal to the speed of sound
exp: When a source moves faster than sound (supersonic), the pressure waves pile into a shock cone, heard on the ground as a sonic boom.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A 300 Hz sound wave travels a distance equal to 150 times its wavelength in time t. The value of t is
exp: Distance = 150λ; speed = fλ = 300λ. Time = distance/speed = 150λ/(300λ) = 0.5 s (the wavelength cancels out).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A sound wave at 330 m/s produces 20 crests and 20 troughs in 0.1 s. Its wavelength is
exp: 20 crests + 20 troughs = 20 complete waves in 0.1 s, so frequency = 20/0.1 = 200 Hz. Wavelength = speed/frequency = 330/200 = 1.65 m.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: In the gamma decay of a nucleus,
options: mass number changes but atomic number does not
mass number does not change but atomic number does
neither the mass number nor the atomic number changes
exp: Gamma decay releases only a high-energy photon as the nucleus drops from an excited to a lower energy state. No nucleons are lost, so both the mass number and atomic number stay the same (only energy is emitted).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Regarding protection of individuals being tried for offences, which statement is not correct?
options: A confession can never be used as evidence against the accused.
The accused must have violated an existing law.
An accused cannot be tried and punished for the same offence again.
The punishment must be as provided in the law existing on the date the offence was committed.
exp: A confession is not automatically barred — only one obtained under coercion is inadmissible; a voluntary confession can be used — so the absolute claim in (a) is false. The others reflect Article 20 safeguards (no ex-post-facto law, no double jeopardy). (A polity item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which radioactive substance(s) enter the human body through the food chain and cause physiological disorders?
exp: Strontium-90 (bone), Iodine-131 (thyroid) and Cesium-137 (soft tissue) are all fission products that enter the food chain and accumulate in the body, causing radiation damage and cancers.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: On the operating principles of reactors vs bombs:
exp: Statement 2 is correct (reactors run controlled chain reactions, bombs uncontrolled) and 3 is treated as correct (reactors operate at criticality). Statement 1 is false (reactors do sustain a chain reaction) and 4 is false (reactors use moderators, bombs do not).
subs: 1. Chain reaction is used in bombs but there is no chain reaction in reactors.
2. In a reactor the reaction is controlled, in bombs uncontrolled.
3. Operating reactors are critical, while there is no question of criticality in a bomb.
4. Reactors do not use moderators while bombs do.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which element is an isobar of calcium (Z = 20, A = 40)?
exp: Isobars have the same mass number but different atomic number. 18 protons + 22 neutrons gives mass number 40 with Z = 18 (argon) — same A = 40 as calcium but different Z, so they are isobars.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering experiment on thin gold foil led to the discovery of
exp: The deflection of a few alpha particles through large angles showed that an atom's positive charge and mass are concentrated in a tiny central nucleus — Rutherford's nuclear model of the atom.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The recent explosion near the OIL well in Baghjan was due to
options: removing the spool during blowout control operations
transfer of oil to a pipeline
leakage of radiation from a radioactive substance
exp: The 2020 Baghjan (Assam) gas well blowout caught fire during well-control operations (removal of the spool), causing a major blaze and ecological damage near Dibru-Saikhowa. (A current-affairs item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is a non-conventional source of energy?
exp: Solar energy is a renewable, non-conventional source. Petroleum, coal and nuclear (radioactive) fuels are conventional/exhaustible sources.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The radioactive isotope of hydrogen is
exp: Hydrogen's three isotopes are protium (¹H), deuterium (²H) and tritium (³H) — only tritium is radioactive (it beta-decays). Hydronium (H₃O⁺) is an ion, not an isotope.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The hydrogen bomb and the uranium bomb are based respectively on
exp: A hydrogen (thermonuclear) bomb releases energy by fusing light nuclei, while a uranium bomb releases energy by fission of heavy nuclei.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: "Qubit" refers to a two-valued quantity used in
exp: A qubit (quantum bit) is the basic unit of information in quantum computers; unlike a classical bit it can exist in a superposition of 0 and 1.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The rest mass of the Higgs boson is estimated to be close to
exp: The Higgs boson discovered at CERN (2012) has a mass of about 125 GeV/c², closest to the 100 GeV option. (0.5 MeV is the electron's mass; ~938 MeV is the proton's.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The pressure exerted by a 760 mm column of mercury at 0 °C is known as
exp: A 760 mm Hg column at 0 °C defines one standard atmosphere (≈101.325 kPa). The pascal is the SI unit of pressure, the bar is 100 kPa, and the poise is a unit of viscosity.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Calcium (atomic number 20) and argon (atomic number 18) both have mass number 40. They are
exp: Isobars have the same mass number but different atomic numbers — exactly the case here (both A = 40, but Z = 20 and 18). Isotopes share atomic number; isotones share neutron number.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The Plum Pudding Model of the atom was proposed by
exp: J. J. Thomson, who discovered the electron, proposed the plum-pudding model — electrons embedded in a sphere of positive charge. Rutherford later replaced it with the nuclear model.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The number of atoms in 46 g of sodium-23 (N = Avogadro constant) is
exp: 46 g of Na-23 is 46/23 = 2 moles, and each mole contains N atoms, giving 2N atoms.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement is not correct?
options: Elements are defined by the number of protons.
Isobars are atoms with the same atomic number but different mass number.
The mass number equals the number of nucleons in the nucleus.
Valency is the combining capacity of an atom.
exp: Statement b actually describes isotopes. Isobars have the same mass number but different atomic numbers, so the definition in b is wrong. The other statements are correct.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: "Atomic number of an element is a more fundamental property than its atomic mass." Who made this statement?
exp: Henry Moseley, through his X-ray work, showed that the atomic number (nuclear charge) — not atomic mass — is the fundamental basis for ordering elements, leading to the modern periodic law.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: If the atomic number of an element is 11, the correct name, symbol and valency are
exp: Atomic number 11 is sodium (Na); with one electron in its outermost shell it has a valency of 1.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The equivalent weight of Ba(OH)₂ (atomic weight of Ba = 137.3) is
exp: Molecular weight of Ba(OH)₂ = 137.3 + 2(16 + 1) = 171.3. Equivalent weight = molecular weight ÷ acidity (number of OH⁻ = 2) = 171.3/2 = 85.7.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The correct order of atomic radius of Li, Na, Be and O is
exp: Radius increases down a group and decreases across a period. Na (period 3) is largest; Li > Be (Be is further right in period 2); O (far right) is smallest. Hence Na > Li > Be > O.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which could not be explained by Rutherford's nuclear model?
options: Presence of nucleus at the centre
Comparison of sizes of atom and nucleus
exp: Rutherford's model could not explain why orbiting electrons, which should continuously radiate energy and spiral into the nucleus, do not — i.e. the stability of the atom. Bohr's model later addressed this with quantised orbits.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Rutherford's α-particle scattering experiment on gold foil is responsible for the discovery of
exp: Large-angle deflection of a few alpha particles revealed a dense, positively charged nucleus at the atom's centre.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Biological catalysts are protein molecules which:
exp: Enzymes speed up reactions (1), emerge unchanged (2), and work best around body temperature 37 °C (3). Statement 4 contradicts the very definition of an enzyme, so it is wrong.
subs: 1. speed up a chemical reaction
2. remain unchanged after reaction
3. function optimally at 37 °C
4. do not have enzymatic activity.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement is correct?
options: The oxidation number of hydrogen is always zero.
Hydrogen can have more than one oxidation number.
exp: Hydrogen is usually +1 (in water, acids) but is −1 in metal hydrides (e.g. NaH) and 0 as H₂ — so it shows more than one oxidation number.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Human insulin has one α-chain (21 amino acids) and one β-chain (30 amino acids). How many functional insulin genes occur in adult humans?
exp: Humans have a single insulin (INS) gene; both chains are produced from one precursor (proinsulin) encoded by that gene and then processed.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: In the balanced equation aFe₂O₃(s) + bCO(g) → cFe(s) + dCO₂(g), the coefficients a, b, c, d respectively are
exp: Balancing gives Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂, so a = 1, b = 3, c = 2, d = 3.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which nitrogen oxide has the highest oxidation state of nitrogen?
exp: Oxidation states of N: NO (+2), NO₂ (+4), N₂O (+1), N₂O₅ (+5) — the highest. (Nitrogen's maximum is +5.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The Kyoto Protocol commits State parties to reduction in
exp: The Kyoto Protocol (1997) legally bound developed countries to cut greenhouse-gas emissions to combat climate change.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement is not correct (molecular projections)?
options: Fischer projection represents the molecule in an eclipsed conformation.
Newman projection can be eclipsed, staggered or skew.
Fischer projection is the molecule's most stable conformation.
In Sawhorse projections, the lines are inclined at 120° to each other.
exp: The Fischer projection depicts an eclipsed arrangement, which is not the most stable conformation (the staggered form is more stable). So statement c is false.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: PCl₅ has a trigonal bipyramidal structure, so the hybridization is
exp: Five bonding pairs in a trigonal bipyramidal geometry require sp³d (dsp³) hybridization (one d orbital with the s and three p orbitals).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The number of water molecules associated with copper sulphate to form crystals is
exp: Blue vitriol is CuSO₄·5H₂O — copper sulphate pentahydrate, with five water molecules of crystallisation.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A mixture of sodium chloride and ammonium chloride can be separated by
exp: Ammonium chloride sublimes on heating (solid → vapour) while sodium chloride does not, so sublimation cleanly separates the two.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not an example of an oxidation reaction?
options: Butter changing taste if left long
A white substance forming when barium chloride solution is mixed with sodium sulphate
exp: Mixing BaCl₂ with Na₂SO₄ gives a precipitation (double-displacement) of BaSO₄ — no change in oxidation states, so it is not oxidation. Rancidity of butter, rusting and wine souring all involve oxidation.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is a feature of the cell membrane?
options: Bilayer of phospholipid molecules in which proteins and cholesterol are embedded
Bilayer of protein molecules in which lipid and cholesterol are embedded
Bilayer of neutral lipid with proteins and cholesterol embedded
Bilayer of neutral lipid lacking cholesterol and proteins
exp: The fluid-mosaic model describes the membrane as a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins and cholesterol. (A biology item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which process leads to expansion of certain minerals as they take up water, stressing the rock?
exp: In hydration, minerals absorb water into their structure and swell, generating stress that helps break the rock — a chemical weathering process. (A geography item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: On heating lead nitrate over a flame:
exp: 2Pb(NO₃)₂ → 2PbO + 4NO₂ + O₂. Colourless O₂ is released (2) and it is thermal decomposition giving NO₂ (4). It is decomposition, not oxidation (3 wrong); and the brown fumes are NO₂, not NO, so statement 1 as written is incorrect.
subs: 1. Brown fumes of NO are released.
2. Colourless O₂ gas is released.
3. It is an oxidation reaction.
4. It is thermal decomposition producing NO₂ gas.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not an oxidation reaction?
exp: Opening soda merely releases dissolved CO₂ — a physical change with no change in oxidation state. Rusting, rancidity and combustion are all oxidation reactions.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The balanced equation for Fe + H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + H₂ is
exp: Balancing Fe (3), O (4) and H (8 on each side) gives 3Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which catalytic system is used to reduce an unsaturated hydrocarbon to a saturated one?
exp: Catalytic hydrogenation adds H₂ across double/triple bonds using a nickel catalyst (as in hardening vegetable oils into vanaspati).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not an example of chemical weathering?
exp: Salt crystal growth is physical (mechanical) weathering — crystals growing in cracks exert pressure. Acid action, hydrolysis and oxidation are chemical weathering. (A geography item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: How many carbon atoms are present in a pyruvate molecule?
exp: Pyruvate (CH₃COCOO⁻) is a 3-carbon molecule — the end product of glycolysis.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The Kyoto Protocol specifically relates to which issue?
exp: The Kyoto Protocol targets the reduction of greenhouse-gas emissions. (Ozone/CFCs are the Montreal Protocol; biodiversity is the CBD.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is the correct chemical formula of a carboxylic acid?
exp: A carboxylic acid contains the –COOH group. C₂H₅COOH (propanoic acid) has it; C₂H₅OH is an alcohol, C₂H₆ an alkane, and CH₃COCH₃ a ketone.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Variable oxidation numbers are possible for
exp: Iron, a transition metal, shows variable oxidation states (+2 and +3). Sodium (+1), lithium (+1) and calcium (+2) have fixed oxidation states.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: In paper manufacturing, degumming of the raw material is done using
exp: Caustic soda (NaOH), a strong alkali, dissolves the gummy lignin/pectin material from plant fibres during pulping.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The pH of a sample of multiple-distilled water is
exp: Pure (distilled) water is neutral, so its pH is about 7 (slightly less in practice if it absorbs CO₂).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Molecular mass of sulphuric acid is 98. If 49 g is dissolved to make one litre of solution, the strength is
exp: Equivalent weight of H₂SO₄ = 98/2 = 49 g. 49 g in 1 L = 1 gram-equivalent per litre = 1 N.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The white material whose paste keeps a fractured bone fixed in place is
exp: Plaster of Paris (CaSO₄·½H₂O) sets into a hard solid on adding water, so it is used in casts to immobilise broken bones.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Accumulation of which substance in a sprinter's muscles causes cramp?
exp: During intense exercise, muscles respire anaerobically, converting glucose to lactic acid, whose build-up causes fatigue and cramps.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Two reactants at room temperature produce a gas that turns limewater milky. The reactants could be
exp: A carbonate + acid releases CO₂, which turns limewater milky. Zinc + HCl gives hydrogen; copper does not react with dilute HCl; methane + oxygen needs ignition.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The reaction of which pair produces hydrogen gas?
exp: A reactive metal + dilute acid gives hydrogen: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. Nitric acid is oxidising (gives nitrogen oxides, not H₂), and a carbonate gives CO₂.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The monomer(s) used to synthesise Nylon 6 is/are
exp: Nylon 6 is made from the single monomer caprolactam. (Hexamethylenediamine + adipic acid give Nylon 6,6.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which acid is also known as Vitamin C?
exp: Vitamin C is ascorbic acid; its deficiency causes scurvy.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A solution with pH equal to zero is
exp: The lower the pH, the more acidic the solution. pH 0 means a very high H⁺ concentration, i.e. a strongly acidic solution.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which acid is produced in the human stomach?
exp: Gastric glands secrete hydrochloric acid, which activates digestive enzymes and kills ingested microbes.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Match: A. Boric acid B. Citric acid C. Magnesium hydroxide D. Acetic acid |
exp: Boric acid → antiseptic; citric acid → food preservative; magnesium hydroxide (milk of magnesia) → antacid; acetic acid (vinegar) → pickle.
subs: 1. Antiseptic
2. Food preservative
3. Antacid
4. Pickle.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The energy currency for cellular processes is
exp: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) stores and supplies energy for cellular work; its hydrolysis to ADP releases usable energy. (A biology item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Match: A. Bleaching powder B. Baking soda C. Washing soda D. Slaked lime |
exp: Bleaching powder = CaOCl₂ (4); baking soda = NaHCO₃ (1); washing soda = Na₂CO₃·10H₂O (2); slaked lime = Ca(OH)₂ (3).
subs: 1. NaHCO₃
2. Na₂CO₃·10H₂O
3. Ca(OH)₂
4. CaOCl₂.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Apart from acid secretion, peptic ulcers also develop from a bacterial infection by
exp: Helicobacter pylori colonises the stomach lining and is the major bacterial cause of peptic ulcers (a discovery that won a Nobel Prize). (A biology item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which plant hormone would you suggest to increase cell division in plants?
exp: Cytokinins promote cell division (cytokinesis) in plants. Abscisic acid inhibits growth, gibberellins promote elongation, and auxins control apical dominance/cell elongation. (A biology item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is used in soda-acid fire extinguishers?
exp: Soda-acid extinguishers mix sodium hydrogen carbonate (NaHCO₃) with sulphuric acid; the reaction releases CO₂, which smothers the fire.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: About universal indicator:
exp: Universal indicator is a blend of dyes (1) that shows a range of colours with H⁺ concentration/pH (2). It estimates pH but is not used for precise titration end-points (sharp single-colour-change indicators are), so statement 3 is not appropriate.
subs: 1. It is a mixture of several indicators.
2. It shows different colours at different concentrations of hydrogen ions.
3. It helps determine the strength of an acid and base in titration.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which mineral acid is found in the human stomach?
exp: The stomach's gastric juice contains the mineral acid HCl (the others listed are organic acids).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which living organism gives litmus?
exp: Litmus dye is extracted from lichens — symbiotic organisms of fungi and algae.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The stinging hair of nettle leaves injects a fluid causing burning pain. The fluid is
exp: Nettle stings inject methanoic acid (formic acid), the same acid found in ant stings, causing the burning sensation.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The atmosphere of Venus is made of thick yellowish clouds of
exp: Venus is shrouded in dense clouds of sulphuric acid droplets above a CO₂-rich atmosphere.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Regarding bile secreted by the liver, which statement is not correct?
options: Bile contains enzymes for digestion of lipids.
Bile neutralizes the acidic pH of food from the stomach.
Bile makes the food alkaline, aiding pancreatic enzymes.
exp: Bile contains no digestive enzymes; it only emulsifies fats (breaks them into droplets) and neutralises stomach acid — so statement a is false. (A biology item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The chemical composition of a soda-acid type fire extinguisher is
options: Solution of sodium hydrogen carbonate and sulfuric acid
exp: A soda-acid extinguisher contains sodium hydrogen carbonate (NaHCO₃) and sulphuric acid, which react to generate the CO₂ that extinguishes the fire.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: While diluting concentrated nitric acid:
exp: The safe rule is to add acid slowly to water (3) with stirring, because dilution is highly exothermic. Adding water to acid (2) can cause violent spattering, and dilution decreases H₃O⁺ per volume, so 1 is also wrong.
subs: 1. the concentration of H₃O⁺ ions per volume increases
2. water must be added slowly to the concentrated acid
3. acid must be added slowly to water.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Identify the soil: contains sand, silt and clay; adequate potash, phosphoric acid and lime; classified on the basis of age.
exp: Alluvial soils are mixtures of sand/silt/clay rich in potash, phosphoric acid and lime, and are classified by age into khadar (new) and bhangar (old). (A geography item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Regarding acids, which statement is not correct?
options: Hydrochloric acid is present in gastric juice.
Acetic acid is the main constituent of vinegar.
Oxalic acid is found in tamarind paste.
Lemon and orange juices contain citric acid and ascorbic acid respectively.
exp: Tamarind contains tartaric acid, not oxalic acid — so statement c is false. The others are correct.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Methanol is toxic because
options: it is oxidised to methanal in the liver, which coagulates the protoplasm
it is oxidised to acetic acid in the liver, which coagulates the protoplasm
it is oxidised to CO in the liver, which coagulates the protoplasm
exp: In the liver methanol is oxidised to methanal (formaldehyde), a toxic compound that coagulates protoplasm/protein, damaging cells (notably the optic nerve, causing blindness).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Vinegar is
options: a 5–8% solution of acetic acid in water
exp: Vinegar is a dilute (≈5–8%) solution of acetic acid in water.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which hormone inhibits growth activity in plants?
exp: Abscisic acid (ABA) is the plant growth inhibitor — it promotes dormancy and stomatal closure. The others are growth promoters. (A biology item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Starch belongs to which category of biomolecules?
exp: Starch is a polysaccharide — a storage carbohydrate made of glucose units. (A biology item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Match: A. Bleaching powder B. Baking soda C. Washing soda D. Plaster of Paris |
exp: Bleaching powder = calcium oxychloride (3); baking soda = sodium bicarbonate (1); washing soda = sodium carbonate decahydrate (2); plaster of Paris = calcium sulphate hydrate (4). (POP is strictly CaSO₄·½H₂O; the source lists "2H₂O".)
subs: 1. Sodium bicarbonate
2. Sodium carbonate, 10H₂O
3. Calcium oxychloride
4. Calcium sulphate, 2H₂O.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is used in the bleaching of paper?
exp: Chlorine (and chlorine compounds such as chlorine dioxide) bleaches paper pulp by oxidising and removing coloured lignin. (The source prints option a as "Chloride"; the intended bleaching agent is chlorine.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not a plant hormone?
exp: Thyroxine is an animal hormone (from the thyroid gland). Gibberellins, abscisic acid and auxins are plant hormones. (A biology item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Enzymes that catalyze the same reaction but have different amino acid compositions are called
exp: Isoenzymes (isozymes) are different molecular forms of an enzyme that catalyse the same reaction but differ in amino-acid sequence (e.g. lactate dehydrogenase variants). (A biology item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A solution with a pH value less than 7 is
exp: On the pH scale, values below 7 are acidic, 7 is neutral and above 7 is basic.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not an allotrope of carbon?
exp: Coal is an impure mixture (mainly carbon with other matter), not a crystalline allotrope. Diamond, graphite and graphene are pure crystalline allotropes of carbon.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Regarding soils:
exp: Black soils (2) and laterite soils (3) are correctly described. Alluvial soils are generally deficient in nitrogen (and humus), so statement 1 is false. (A geography item.)
subs: 1. Alluvial soils are rich in nitrogen.
2. Black soils are rich in iron and lime but deficient in nitrogen.
3. Laterite soils are rich in iron and aluminium but deficient in nitrogen and potassium.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement is not correct (about potassium bromate)?
options: CSE found some pre-packaged breads tested positive for potassium bromate/iodate.
FSSAI recommended removing potassium bromate from permissible additives.
The government banned potassium bromate as a food additive.
exp: Potassium bromate is classified as a possible carcinogen, not a neurotoxin — so statement d is false. The CSE finding, the FSSAI recommendation and the subsequent ban are all correct. (A current-affairs item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Match: A. TISCO B. BALCO C. BPCL D. BEL |
exp: TISCO → Iron & Steel (2); BALCO → Aluminium (4); BPCL → Chemicals/petroleum (1); BEL (Bharat Electronics) → Electronics (3). (A general-knowledge item.)
subs: 1. Chemicals
2. Iron & Steel
3. Electronics
4. Aluminium.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A copper wire of length l, area A carrying current I dissipates power P. An aluminium wire of identical dimensions carrying the same current dissipates
exp: Power = I²R, and R ∝ resistivity. Aluminium's resistivity (~2.8 ×10⁻⁸ Ω·m) is roughly 1.7 times copper's (~1.7 ×10⁻⁸), so for the same current the aluminium wire dissipates more power — closest to the "2P" option.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not true for diamond?
options: It has the same percentage of carbon as graphite.
It is a better electric conductor than graphite.
It has a different carbon-to-carbon distance in all directions.
exp: Diamond is an electrical insulator (all four valence electrons are locked in covalent bonds), whereas graphite conducts (it has delocalised electrons). So statement c is false.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: In graphite, each carbon atom is bonded to three other carbon atoms
options: in the same plane giving a hexagonal array
in the same plane giving a square array
in the same plane giving a pentagonal array
exp: Graphite has carbon in flat layers of hexagonal rings; the fourth electron is delocalised (giving conductivity), and weak forces between layers make it slippery.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Silver articles turn black after some time in air because
options: silver reacts with moist CO₂ to form silver carbonate
silver reacts with sulphur in the air to form a coating of silver sulphide
silver reacts with nitrogen oxides to form silver nitrate
exp: Atmospheric hydrogen sulphide/sulphur reacts with silver to form black silver sulphide (Ag₂S) — the tarnish on silverware.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which oxide shows both acidic and basic behaviour?
exp: Zinc oxide is amphoteric — it reacts with both acids and bases. MgO and CaO are basic oxides.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Aluminium is manufactured from
exp: Bauxite (hydrated aluminium oxide) is the chief ore of aluminium; it is refined to alumina and then electrolysed.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Silver articles react with which substance, making them black?
exp: Silver reacts with sulphur compounds in air to form black silver sulphide, the familiar tarnish.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which element is a non-metal but is lustrous?
exp: Iodine is a non-metal that has a metallic (shiny) lustre. (Silicon and germanium are metalloids; graphite carbon is lustrous but carbon is the broader option — iodine is the textbook example of a lustrous non-metal.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which carbon allotrope(s) are good conductors of electricity?
exp: Only graphite conducts well, thanks to its delocalised electrons. Diamond is an insulator, and fullerene is at best a poor/semi-conductor.
subs: 1. Diamond
2. Graphite
3. Fullerene.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: When copper reacts with moist carbon dioxide in air, it forms a green coating of
exp: Copper develops a green basic cupric carbonate coating (patina) when exposed to moist CO₂ — as seen on old copper statues.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: In joining railway tracks, iron oxide is made to react with
exp: This is the thermite reaction: Fe₂O₃ + 2Al → 2Fe + Al₂O₃ + great heat, producing molten iron that welds the rail joints.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not true of the anodizing process?
options: Aluminium, titanium and magnesium can be anodized.
Clean aluminium is the anode and oxygen gas is evolved at the cathode.
It is used in the aircraft industry.
exp: In anodizing, the aluminium article is the anode, where oxygen is liberated and a thick protective oxide forms — so saying oxygen evolves "at the cathode" is wrong.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: For the reaction of Fe₂O₃ with aluminium:
exp: It is the thermite reaction (1) whose intense heat is used for welding (2). Aluminium is the reducing agent (not oxidizing), so 3 is wrong; the products are molten Fe and Al₂O₃ (not Al), so 4 is wrong.
subs: 1. It is the thermite reaction.
2. The heat evolved is used for welding.
3. Aluminium acts as an oxidizing agent.
4. Molten Fe and Al are formed at the end.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement about diamond and graphite is correct?
options: They have similar physical and chemical properties.
Diamond is hard but graphite is smooth and slippery.
exp: Though both are pure carbon, their structures differ: diamond's rigid 3-D network makes it the hardest natural material, while graphite's layered sheets slide easily, making it soft and slippery (and conducting).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Potassium nitrate is not used
options: as a preservative of meat products
