exp: Potassium nitrate is used as a fertiliser and in gunpowder, and has medicinal/dental uses (e.g. toothpaste for sensitivity). Meat is usually preserved with sodium nitrate/nitrite, not potassium nitrate - so 'as a preservative of meat products' (option d) is the intended wrong use.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Tooth enamel of humans is made up of
exp: Tooth enamel is mainly hydroxyapatite, a form of calcium phosphate — the hardest substance in the body. (Partly a biology item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Arrange the major elements of the Earth's crust in ascending order of weight percentage:
exp: Crustal abundance (by weight): Calcium (~4%) < Aluminium (~8%) < Silicon (~28%) < Oxygen (~46%) — so ascending order is 2, 1, 3, 4. (A geology/geography item.)
subs: 1. Aluminium
2. Calcium
3. Silicon
4. Oxygen.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A yellow flame with lots of black smoke while burning a hydrocarbon fuel means the fuel is
exp: Unsaturated hydrocarbons (with double/triple bonds) have a high carbon content and burn with incomplete combustion, giving a sooty yellow flame with black smoke (unburnt carbon).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: For CaO(s) + H₂O(l) → Ca(OH)₂(aq) + Heat:
exp: Slaked lime [Ca(OH)₂] solution is used for whitewashing (2) and it is an inorganic compound (4). The whitewash sets because Ca(OH)₂ (not CaO) reacts with CO₂ to form CaCO₃, so statements 1 and 3 are wrong.
subs: 1. Quicklime is used for whitewashing.
2. The solution of slaked lime is used for whitewashing.
3. CaO reacts slowly with CO₂ to form a thin layer of CaCO₃ on walls.
4. Calcium hydroxide, called slaked lime, is an inorganic compound.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement is not correct for benzene?
options: Each carbon forms sigma bonds with two other carbons at a bond angle of 120°.
Delocalized electrons form a symmetrical cloud above and below the plane.
The C–C bond length is intermediate between single and double bonds.
exp: Benzene is a single, symmetric resonance-stabilised structure — the claim that "it has six isomers" is false. The 120° bond angles, the delocalised π-cloud, and the intermediate C–C bond length are all correct.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Dolomite powder applied to agricultural land is meant to
options: increase the pH of the soil
lower the pH of the soil
exp: Dolomite (calcium-magnesium carbonate) is a liming material that neutralises acidity, raising the pH of acidic soils.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: An emulsion consists of
exp: An emulsion is a colloid of two immiscible liquids (e.g. oil dispersed in water, as in milk).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: In desalination of seawater by reverse osmosis, the pressure applied to the solution is
exp: In reverse osmosis, an external pressure greater than the osmotic pressure is applied so that water is forced from the concentrated (salty) side to the pure side through the membrane.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A soap solution used for cleaning appears cloudy because soap micelles
exp: Soap micelles are colloidal-sized particles that scatter light (the Tyndall effect), making the solution look cloudy/translucent.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: From which factory site were limestone and chert blades mass-produced and sent to Harappan settlements in Sindh?
exp: The Rohri/Sukkur Hills in Sindh were a major source of chert, where blades were mass-produced and distributed to Harappan sites. (Khetri was a copper source.) (A history item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Regarding ozone, which statement is not correct?
options: Ozone is found mostly at 15–55 km in the atmosphere.
Ozone is produced by gaseous chemical reactions.
16th November is the International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer.
Ozone is a form of oxygen with three oxygen atoms bonded together.
exp: The International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer is 16th September, not 16th November — so statement c is false. The others correctly describe stratospheric ozone (O₃).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Osmosis is the movement of water molecules from
options: higher to lower concentration through a cell wall
lower to higher concentration through a fully permeable membrane
higher to lower concentration through a fully permeable membrane
higher to lower concentration through a semi-permeable membrane
exp: Osmosis is the movement of water from a region of higher water concentration to lower water concentration across a semi-permeable membrane (which lets water but not solute pass).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which air pollutant combines with haemoglobin and reduces its oxygen-carrying capacity, causing suffocation and possibly death?
exp: Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin ~200 times more strongly than oxygen, forming carboxyhaemoglobin and starving tissues of oxygen.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The main constituents of biogas are
exp: Biogas is chiefly methane (~50–70%) with carbon dioxide, produced by anaerobic decomposition of organic matter.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The foul smell of urine spilled on the floor is mainly due to bacterial decomposition of
exp: Bacteria break down urea into ammonia, whose pungent smell causes the characteristic odour.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which greenhouse gas has the maximum average residence time in the atmosphere?
exp: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are extremely stable and persist for many decades to over a century in the atmosphere — far longer than methane (~12 yr) or water vapour (days).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The ozone hole is a region over
options: the Antarctic, caused mainly by CFC gases
the Antarctic, caused mainly by CO₂
the Arctic, caused mainly by CFC gases
the Arctic, caused mainly by CO₂
exp: The seasonal ozone hole forms over Antarctica, where chlorine from CFCs (activated on polar stratospheric clouds) destroys ozone.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: In cancer cells (unlike normal regulated cells),
options: there is breakdown of regulatory mechanisms leading to benign and malignant tumours
controlled cell division and over-production of genetic material occur
RNA is mutated and produced in less amount
DNA is mutated and produced in less amount
exp: Cancer arises when the controls on cell growth and division break down, causing uncontrolled proliferation that forms benign or malignant tumours. The other options misstate the mechanism.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Match: A. Mitochondria B. Chloroplast C. Ribosomes D. Lysosomes |
exp: Mitochondria → ATP formation (4); chloroplast → photosynthesis (1); ribosomes → protein synthesis (2); lysosomes → intracellular digestion (3).
subs: 1. Photosynthesis
2. Protein synthesis
3. Intracellular digestion
4. ATP formation.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Lysosomes are formed from which cell organelle?
exp: Lysosomes bud off from the Golgi apparatus, which packages the hydrolytic (digestive) enzymes they contain.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A protein made on bound-ER ribosomes targets the inner thylakoid space of a chloroplast. How many membranes must it cross?
exp: To reach the thylakoid lumen the protein must cross the outer chloroplast envelope, the inner chloroplast envelope, and the thylakoid membrane — three membranes in all.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which function is not carried out by the smooth endoplasmic reticulum?
exp: Protein synthesis occurs on the rough ER (which bears ribosomes). The smooth ER lacks ribosomes and handles lipid/steroid synthesis, detoxification and transport.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which organelle mainly functions as a storehouse of digestive enzymes?
exp: Lysosomes are membrane-bound sacs packed with hydrolytic (digestive) enzymes used for intracellular digestion.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement about histone proteins is correct?
options: Present in the nucleus in association with DNA
Associated with lipids in the cytosol
Associated with carbohydrates in the cytosol
exp: Histones are nuclear proteins around which DNA wraps to form nucleosomes, packaging the genome into chromatin.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Chlorophyll in photosynthetic prokaryotic bacteria is associated with
exp: Prokaryotes have no plastids/chloroplasts, so their photosynthetic pigments are housed in infoldings of the plasma membrane (membranous vesicles/chromatophores).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which cell organelle is known as the "suicide bag" of a cell?
exp: Lysosomes are called "suicide bags" because their digestive enzymes can break down the cell's own contents (autolysis) when it is damaged or dying.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not found in animal cells?
exp: A cell wall is characteristic of plant cells (and fungi/bacteria), not animal cells, which have only a flexible plasma membrane.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which cell organelle contains DNA?
exp: Mitochondria (and chloroplasts) have their own DNA — a remnant of their endosymbiotic origin — besides the nucleus.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Under Kingdom Plantae, which group is predominantly aquatic?
exp: Algae are largely aquatic (freshwater and marine) plants. Bryophytes need moist land, while pteridophytes and gymnosperms are terrestrial.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Antibiotics such as penicillin block
exp: Penicillin inhibits bacterial cell-wall (peptidoglycan) synthesis, so the bacteria burst. Human cells lack cell walls, which is why penicillin is selectively toxic to bacteria.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Cell wall is not present in the cells of
exp: Animal (human) cells have no cell wall — only a plasma membrane. Bacteria, plants and fungi all possess cell walls (of different compositions).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which cell organelles have their own DNA and ribosomes?
exp: Mitochondria and plastids (e.g. chloroplasts) are semi-autonomous organelles with their own DNA and ribosomes — evidence of their endosymbiotic origin.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: About fission:
exp: "Fission" has two valid senses: biological fission (a unicellular organism dividing, 1) and nuclear fission (a heavy nucleus splitting into lighter ones, 2). Statement 3 describes fusion, not fission.
subs: 1. It relates to creation of new individuals by cell division in unicellular organisms.
2. It relates to transformation of heavier nuclei into smaller nuclei.
3. It relates to creating a heavier nucleus by combining two nuclei.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement about the cell membrane is correct?
options: It is permeable to all substances.
It is flexible and enables the cell to engulf materials.
It does not allow diffusion of gases.
exp: The membrane is a flexible phospholipid bilayer, allowing processes like endocytosis (engulfing). It is selectively permeable (not made of cellulose, not permeable to all, and it does allow gas diffusion).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: In plant cells, RNA is present in
options: nuclei, cytoplasm, mitochondria, chloroplast and ribosomes
exp: RNA is found wherever transcription/translation or organellar genomes exist — in the nucleus, cytoplasm, ribosomes, mitochondria and chloroplasts of a plant cell.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: In a labelled plant-cell diagram (parts 1–5), which option correctly identifies them?
exp: From the outside in, a plant cell shows the cell wall (1), then the cell membrane (2), with the endoplasmic reticulum (3), a large vacuole (4) and the nucleus (5) inside — matching option b. (Figure-based.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is the correct combination of organelles and functions?
options: Mitochondria-Respiration, Chloroplast-Photosynthesis, Ribosome-Protein Synthesis, RER-Transport of proteins
exp: Correct pairings: mitochondria → respiration, chloroplast → photosynthesis, ribosome → protein synthesis, rough ER → transport of proteins — option a.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Cell wall is absent in which organism?
exp: A tapeworm is an animal (flatworm), and animal cells lack cell walls. Bacteria, diatoms (silica wall) and mushrooms (fungal, chitin wall) all have cell walls.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which organelle in animal cells can digest foreign materials?
exp: Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes that break down ingested/foreign material and worn-out organelles.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The only structure in a leaf that hosts chlorophyll is the
exp: Chlorophyll is located in chloroplasts, the organelles where photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Why does the rough endoplasmic reticulum look rough under a microscope?
options: Presence of ribosomes on its surface
exp: The studding of ribosomes on its outer surface gives the rough ER its granular ("rough") appearance and its role in protein synthesis.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Sponges belong to which phylum?
exp: Sponges are phylum Porifera — pore-bearing, sessile, multicellular animals lacking true tissues.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is the correct scheme for classification of animals?
exp: The descending taxonomic hierarchy is Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species (within Kingdom).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which organelle can be seen in a prokaryotic cell?
exp: Prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles and a true nucleus, but they do contain ribosomes (70S) for protein synthesis.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The HIV virus weakens immunity because it destroys
exp: HIV attacks CD4 helper T-lymphocytes, crippling the immune system and leading to AIDS.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Development of an embryo without fertilization is called:
exp: All three are forms of apomixis (embryo formation without fertilization) — parthenogenesis (from an unfertilized egg), apogamy (from gametophyte cells) and sporophytic budding/adventive embryony (from sporophytic tissue).
subs: 1. Parthenogenesis
2. Apogamy
3. Sporophytic budding.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which hormone is essential for the uptake of glucose by cells?
exp: Insulin (from the pancreas) promotes glucose uptake by cells and lowers blood sugar; its deficiency causes diabetes.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Altitude sickness occurs at high altitude due to
options: high partial pressure of carbon dioxide
exp: At high altitude the partial pressure of oxygen is low, so less oxygen diffuses into the blood, causing breathlessness, headache and altitude sickness.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Match (alkaline-earth metals): A. Mg B. Ca C. Sr D. Ba |
exp: Mg → in chlorophyll, traps sunlight (3); Ca → muscle contraction (4); Sr → crimson-red flame colour (1); Ba → barium sulphate to image the gut (2).
subs: 1. Gives red colour to flame
2. Sulphate used in medicine to examine the alimentary canal
3. Traps the energy of sunlight in photosynthesis
4. Control of muscle contraction.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Bleeding gums, falling teeth, fragile bones and delayed wound healing occur due to deficiency of
exp: These are symptoms of scurvy, caused by Vitamin C deficiency (vitamin C is needed for collagen synthesis).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The mammalian heart is myogenic; the heartbeat originates from the
exp: The sinoatrial (SA) node is the heart's natural pacemaker, generating the impulses that set the heart rate.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A footballer diagnosed with growth-hormone deficiency in childhood who won three European Golden Shoes is
exp: Lionel Messi was treated for growth-hormone deficiency as a child and later won multiple European Golden Shoes. (A general-knowledge item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which 12th-century Sanskrit scholar first compiled the Nibandhas (digests of epic and Puranic texts)?
exp: Lakshmidhara, minister of the Gahadavala king Govindachandra, compiled the great digest Krtyakalpataru. (A history item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Consider the following statements:
options: Both true, II not the explanation
exp: Tundra has low biodiversity (I) precisely because its short, cold growing/reproductive season (II) limits the species that can survive — so II correctly explains I. (A geography item.)
subs: Statement I: In a tundra climate, biodiversity is comparatively less.
Statement II: Tundra has a shorter reproductive warm period.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which roles are played by the epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicles and prostate in human reproduction?
exp: Sperms are produced in the testes; these accessory structures handle maturation, storage, transport and providing fluid/nutrients that confer motility. So the correct combination is maturation and motility.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement about haemoglobin is correct?
options: It can carry only oxygen, not carbon dioxide.
It can carry both oxygen and carbon dioxide.
It can carry only carbon dioxide.
It is used only for blood clotting.
exp: Haemoglobin carries oxygen (as oxyhaemoglobin) from lungs to tissues and also transports some CO₂ (as carbaminohaemoglobin) back to the lungs.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement is correct?
options: Urea is produced in the liver.
Urea is produced in the blood.
Urea is produced from digestion of starch.
Urea is produced in lung and kidney.
exp: The liver makes urea from ammonia (a toxic by-product of protein metabolism) via the urea cycle; the kidneys then excrete it.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The correct sequence of events in sexual reproduction in plants is
options: Seedling, embryo, pollination, fertilization, zygote division
Embryo, seedling, pollination, fertilization, zygote division
Pollination, fertilization, division of zygote, formation of embryo, seedling
Seedling, embryo, zygote division, pollination, fertilization
exp: The logical order is pollination → fertilization → zygote divides → embryo forms → seedling develops.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The first enzyme to mix with food in the digestive tract is
exp: Digestion begins in the mouth with salivary amylase (ptyalin), which starts breaking down starch — so it is the first enzyme to act on food.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The correct sequence of organs in the path of urine flow is
exp: Urine forms in the kidney, travels down the ureter to the urinary bladder for storage, and leaves the body through the urethra.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which endocrine gland is not found in pairs in humans?
exp: The pituitary is a single, unpaired midline gland. Adrenals, testes and ovaries occur as pairs.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is a free-living animal?
exp: Planaria is a free-living flatworm. Liver fluke, Wuchereria and Plasmodium are all parasites.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement about variations is not true?
options: Variation is minimum in asexual reproduction.
All variations in a species have equal chances of survival.
Changes in genetic constitution result in variation.
Variants can be selected by environmental factors.
exp: Not all variations are equally likely to survive — natural selection favours advantageous ones — so statement b is false. The others correctly describe variation and selection.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Match: A. Pulmonary artery B. Capillaries C. Coronary artery D. Pulmonary vein |
exp: Pulmonary artery → heart to lungs (4); capillaries → connect arteries and veins (3); coronary artery → supplies the heart muscle (2); pulmonary vein → lungs to heart (1).
subs: 1. Carries blood from lungs to heart
2. Carries blood to heart muscle
3. Connection between arteries and veins
4. Carries blood from heart to lungs.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Hyphae are
options: thin threads formed by many fungi
responsible for preventing water loss in wet conditions
exp: Hyphae are the fine filamentous threads that make up the body (mycelium) of most fungi.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which part of the human alimentary canal can be of maximum length?
exp: The small intestine is the longest part of the alimentary canal (about 6–7 m), maximising the surface area for digestion and absorption.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Blood pressure 120/80 mmHg represents the pressure at
options: ventricular contraction and ventricular relaxation respectively
ventricular contraction and auricular contraction respectively
exp: 120 mmHg is systolic pressure (ventricular contraction) and 80 mmHg is diastolic pressure (ventricular relaxation).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which sequence correctly represents a reflex arc?
options: Receptor → Sensory neuron → Relay neuron (spinal cord) → Brain → Motor neuron → Effector
Receptor → Sensory neuron → Brain → Relay neuron → Motor neuron → Effector
Receptor → Motor neuron → Relay neuron → Sensory neuron → Effector
Receptor → Motor neuron → Brain → Sensory neuron → Effector
exp: A reflex follows Receptor → Sensory (afferent) neuron → relay neuron in the spinal cord → Motor (efferent) neuron → Effector (option a has the correct afferent-to-efferent order; the rapid spinal pathway lets the body respond before the brain processes it).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is essential for the thyroid gland to make thyroxine?
exp: Iodine is a key component of thyroxine (T4/T3); its deficiency causes goitre and hypothyroidism.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: An antibacterial enzyme present in saliva and tears is called
exp: Lysozyme, found in tears, saliva and mucus, digests bacterial cell walls, providing a first line of defence.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The pulse is felt due to the rhythmic contraction and relaxation of the
exp: Each heartbeat sends a pressure wave through the aorta and major arteries, whose rhythmic expansion is felt as the pulse.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which instrument is used to measure blood pressure manually?
exp: A sphygmomanometer (with a cuff and mercury/aneroid gauge) measures arterial blood pressure.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The four human blood types in ABO typing are
exp: The ABO system has four blood groups — A, B, AB and O — based on the A and B antigens present on red cells.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not a part of the male reproductive system in humans?
exp: The cervix is part of the female reproductive system (the neck of the uterus). The prostate, testis and scrotum are male organs.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The inner lining of the human small intestine has numerous finger-like projections called
exp: Villi (and microvilli) greatly increase the small intestine's surface area for efficient absorption of digested food.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which element is essential for the formation of chlorophyll in green plants?
exp: Magnesium is the central atom of the chlorophyll molecule, so it is essential for chlorophyll synthesis (iron is needed for the enzymes but is not part of chlorophyll itself).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: In which process does excess water escape from a plant as droplets?
exp: Guttation is the loss of liquid water as droplets from leaf margins (through hydathodes), typically at night when root pressure is high. Transpiration loses water as vapour.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: If the xylem of a plant is mechanically blocked, which function is affected?
exp: Xylem carries water and dissolved minerals (solutes) upward from roots, so blocking it disrupts both.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which agent does not contribute to seed dispersal?
exp: Seeds are dispersed by wind, water and animals, but fungi play no role in carrying seeds.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement about the growth of coral reefs is not correct?
options: Coral can grow abundantly in fresh-water.
It requires shallow saltwater, not deeper than ~50 m.
It requires plenty of sunlight for photosynthesis.
exp: Corals need warm, shallow, sunlit saltwater and cannot survive in fresh water — so statement a is false. (A geography item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which describes active transport?
options: Movement of a substance against a diffusion gradient using energy from respiration
Against a gradient using energy from photosynthesis
Along a gradient using energy from respiration
exp: Active transport moves substances against their concentration gradient and requires metabolic energy (ATP, from respiration) — distinguishing it from passive diffusion.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement about phloem is correct?
options: Phloem gives support to the plant.
exp: Phloem translocates food (sugars made in photosynthesis) from leaves to the rest of the plant. (Water/minerals are carried by xylem; phloem is a complex tissue.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: To verify whether a tall plant is the progeny of two tall parents or one tall and one short parent, the method is
exp: Self-pollinating the tall plant reveals its genotype: a heterozygous (Tt) plant will produce some short offspring, whereas a homozygous (TT) plant yields only tall ones — confirming the parentage.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Plants prepare glucose in the process of
exp: In photosynthesis, plants use light energy to combine CO₂ and water into glucose and oxygen.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Water rises through xylem in tall trees. The process and water properties that help are
exp: Water loss from leaves creates a transpiration pull, and the cohesion (water–water) and adhesion (water–xylem wall) of water molecules keep the column intact as it is drawn up (the cohesion-tension theory).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not a micronutrient for plants?
exp: Magnesium is a macronutrient (needed in larger amounts, e.g. for chlorophyll). Iron, manganese and chlorine are micronutrients (needed in trace amounts).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Xylem in plants is responsible for the transport of
exp: Xylem conducts water and dissolved mineral salts upward from the roots. (Food is transported by phloem.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not a feature of xerophytes?
exp: Xerophytes (desert plants) reduce stomata to minimise water loss — so "large number of stomata" is wrong. Small leaves, waxy cuticle and sunken stomata are all water-conserving adaptations.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Halophytes are plants that grow on which type of soil?
exp: Halophytes are salt-tolerant plants (e.g. mangroves) adapted to grow in saline soils.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not a part of the vascular bundle in plants?
exp: A vascular bundle consists of xylem, phloem and (in dicots) cambium. The endodermis is a layer of the cortex, not part of the vascular bundle.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A polynucleotide chain of DNA contains
options: a nitrogenous base, deoxyribose sugar and phosphate group
a nitrogenous base, ribose sugar and phosphate group
deoxyribose sugar, ribose sugar and phosphate group
a nitrogenous base and phosphate group only
exp: Each DNA nucleotide is made of a nitrogenous base, a deoxyribose sugar and a phosphate group. (Ribose sugar belongs to RNA.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Copying genetic information from one strand of DNA into RNA is termed
exp: Transcription is the synthesis of RNA from a DNA template. (Translation makes protein from mRNA; replication copies DNA to DNA.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Most viruses that infect plants possess
exp: The majority of plant viruses have single-stranded RNA genomes (e.g. Tobacco Mosaic Virus).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement about the Gupta period is not correct?
options: Sanskrit literature reached classical excellence under royal patronage.
The status of women was redefined — entitled to formal education, became teachers, given right to property, and early marriage prohibited.
Land grants with fiscal/administrative immunities decentralized authority.
Land grants paved the way for feudal developments and serfdom.
exp: In the Gupta period the status of women actually declined — early marriage became common and women's independent rights shrank — so statement b is false. (A history item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement explains the higher mutation rate and faster evolution of RNA viruses?
options: RNA is relatively unstable compared to DNA.
A virus multiplies only within a host cell.
Metabolic processes are absent in viruses.
A virus can remain latent for a long period.
exp: RNA replication lacks proofreading and RNA is chemically less stable, so RNA viruses accumulate mutations quickly and evolve faster.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: According to the Manusmriti, women can acquire wealth through which means?
exp: Among the recognised forms of a woman's wealth (stridhana), the Manusmriti includes gifts given out of affection (e.g. at marriage, from family). (A history item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A food chain is
options: exchange of genetic material between two organisms
the passage of food and thus energy from one organism to another
exp: A food chain describes how food (and the energy in it) is transferred from producers to successive consumers — one trophic level to the next.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: In humans, the chromosomes that determine the birth of a normal female child are
options: one X from mother and one X from father
one X from mother and one Y from father
two X from mother and one X from father
one X and one Y from father and one X from mother
exp: A female is XX — she receives one X from the mother and one X from the father (the father's X-bearing sperm determines a girl).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: An antibiotic is not useful against a virus, but a vaccine is. The most appropriate reason is
options: An antibiotic can break only RNA, but a virus has DNA.
An antibiotic is a carbohydrate, a vaccine a protein that kills the virus.
Only a vaccine can break the genetic material of a virus.
A virus does not use biochemical pathways that antibiotics block, but a vaccine boosts the immune system to fight the virus.
exp: Antibiotics target bacterial metabolic processes, which viruses lack, so they don't work on viruses. A vaccine primes the immune system to recognise and fight the virus.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A mutation in a virus is caused due to a change in its
exp: A mutation is a change in the genetic material (DNA or RNA) of the virus, altering its proteins/behaviour.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Chromosomes are composed of DNA and
exp: Chromosomes are made of DNA wrapped around histone proteins (together called chromatin).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Bacteria have an undefined nuclear region lacking a nuclear membrane, containing only DNA without proteins. This region is called
exp: The nucleoid is the irregular region in a prokaryotic cell where the genetic material lies, with no surrounding membrane.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: "Photo 51" refers to an image of
exp: Photo 51 is Rosalind Franklin's famous X-ray diffraction image of DNA, which was crucial in revealing its double-helix structure.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement about research centres in India is not correct?
options: Rajiv Gandhi Centre for Biotechnology is located at Kolkata.
Central Arid Zone Research Institute is at Jodhpur.
Centre for Social Forestry and Eco-Rehabilitation is at Allahabad.
Institute of Forest Productivity is at Ranchi.
exp: The Rajiv Gandhi Centre for Biotechnology is at Thiruvananthapuram (Kerala), not Kolkata — so statement a is false. (A general-knowledge item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: On ICAR's genome-edited rice varieties:
exp: DRR Rice 100 (Kamla) was developed by ICAR-IIRR, Hyderabad (only Pusa DST Rice 1 is from ICAR-IARI), so statement 1 is wrong. Statement 2 is correct — Kamla, derived from Samba Mahsuri, matures earlier.
subs: 1. DRR Rice 100 (Kamla) and Pusa DST Rice 1 have both been developed by ICAR-IARI, New Delhi.
2. DRR Rice 100 (Kamla), based on Samba Mahsuri, has a shorter duration of maturity.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Transmission of HIV infection generally occurs through
options: transfusion of contaminated blood and blood products
shaking hands with an infected person
exp: HIV spreads through infected blood (and blood products), unprotected sex, shared needles and mother-to-child — not through casual contact, food or air.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Kwashiorkor in children is caused by
options: sufficient carbohydrates and fats but deficient proteins
exp: Kwashiorkor is a protein-deficiency disease (enough calories from carbs/fats but too little protein), marked by oedema and a swollen belly.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Consider the following statements:
options: Both true, II not the explanation
exp: TB risk rises in crowds because the bacteria spread via airborne droplets from coughing/sneezing — so II correctly explains I.
subs: Statement I: A person may suffer from tuberculosis if she/he frequently visits crowded places.
Statement II: TB bacteria spread through droplets by sneezing/coughing.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The special milk produced by a lactating mother, essential for the newborn's immune response, is
options: breast milk produced after a month
exp: Colostrum, the first thick yellowish milk, is rich in antibodies (IgA) and confers passive immunity to the newborn.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which virus was responsible for the recent death of lions in Gir National Park?
exp: Canine Distemper Virus (CDV), along with babesiosis, was linked to the 2018 deaths of Asiatic lions in Gir. (A current-affairs item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not an epidemic disease?
exp: Elephantiasis (lymphatic filariasis) is a chronic, slowly developing parasitic disease, not one that spreads as a sudden epidemic like cholera, malaria or smallpox.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Who introduced the concept of immunization to the medical world?
exp: Edward Jenner developed the first vaccine (against smallpox, using cowpox) and is regarded as the father of immunization.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which Indian institute was approved by the DCGI for human trials of the Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine candidate?
exp: The Serum Institute of India (Pune) partnered to manufacture and trial the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine (Covishield). (A current-affairs item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: An infection constantly maintained at a baseline level in a geographic area without external input is
exp: An endemic disease is one persistently present at a steady, expected level in a particular region (e.g. malaria in some areas).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Rickets develops in children due to deficiency of
exp: Vitamin D deficiency impairs calcium absorption, causing soft, deformed bones — rickets in children.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Yeast, used to make bread, belongs to the group
exp: Yeast is a single-celled fungus; its fermentation of sugars releases CO₂ that makes bread rise.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: During 2020–21, which sector witnessed positive growth despite COVID-19?
options: Electricity, gas, water supply and other utility services
Financial, real estate and professional services
Public administration, defence and other services
exp: In 2020–21, when most sectors contracted, agriculture and the "electricity, gas, water supply & utilities" sector recorded positive growth. (An economics item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Deficiency of iron causes
exp: Iron deficiency reduces haemoglobin production, causing anaemia (fatigue, pallor, breathlessness).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is/are objectives of the Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY)?
exp: PMSSY aims to correct regional imbalances in tertiary healthcare (1) (by setting up AIIMS-like institutions) and augment medical education (3). Universal immunization/health coverage (2) is not its stated objective. (A governance item.)
subs: 1. Correcting regional imbalances in tertiary health care.
2. Universal access to public health services and universal immunization.
3. Augmenting facilities for quality medical education.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Wholesale Price inflation rose in India during 2021–22 due to:
exp: Rising crude oil prices (1), supply-chain disruption (3) and high freight costs (4) drove WPI inflation. Statement 2 is wrong — economic activity was recovering, not falling. (An economics item.)
subs: 1. Sharp increase in international crude oil prices.
2. Decrease in economic activity post-Covid.
3. Disruption of global supply chains.
4. High freight cost.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is/are correct about vaccination against an infectious disease?
exp: A vaccine works by stimulating the body to produce antibodies (and memory cells) (2). It does not physically block entry (1), nor does the vaccine itself kill the pathogen (3) — the primed immune system does that.
subs: 1. It blocks the entry of the infectious agent.
2. It produces antibodies against infection.
3. It kills the infectious agent when it enters the body.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The causal organism of dengue fever is a mosquito-borne virus belonging to which category?
exp: Dengue is caused by the dengue virus, a Flavivirus (an RNA "flavi-ribo" virus), transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: What is the purpose of a firewall?
options: Preventing unauthorised computer access via the internet
Installing software that can harm the computer
Recording everything done on the computer
Running checks to prevent virus attacks
exp: A firewall monitors and controls network traffic to block unauthorised access to/from a computer or network. (An IT item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is an example of an airborne disease?
exp: Tuberculosis spreads through air (droplets from coughing/sneezing). Malaria and dengue are mosquito-borne; cholera is water-borne.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which platform digitizes vaccination records for pregnant women and children up to 16 years, marking a transformative step in India's immunization?
exp: U-WIN is the digital platform (modelled on Co-WIN) that records and tracks routine immunization for pregnant women and children. (A current-affairs item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Plant growth regulators are small, simple molecules of diverse chemical composition. They are
options: indole compounds, adenine derivatives, carotenoids and terpenes
vitamin C, vitamin D and glucose
exp: Plant hormones are chemically varied — auxins (indole compounds), cytokinins (adenine derivatives), abscisic acid (carotenoid-derived) and gibberellins (terpenes).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: How many hydrogen atoms are contained in 1.50 g of glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆)?
exp: Moles of glucose = 1.5/180 = 0.00833. Each molecule has 12 H, so moles of H = 0.1; atoms = 0.1 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 6.02 × 10²².

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which polymer does not contain glucose units?
exp: Glycogen, starch and cellulose are all glucose polymers. Natural rubber is a polymer of isoprene, not glucose.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The number of moles of oxygen gas used in the complete combustion of 1 mole of glucose is
exp: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O — six moles of O₂ are required.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement about starch and glycogen is correct?
options: Both are found in plant cells.
Both are found in animal cells.
Starch is in plant cells and glycogen in animal cells.
Both are present in plant as well as animal cells.
exp: Starch is the storage carbohydrate of plants; glycogen is the storage carbohydrate of animals (and fungi).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Lactose is made up of
exp: Lactose (milk sugar) is a disaccharide of glucose + galactose. (Sucrose = glucose + fructose.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which represent disaccharides?
exp: Maltose and lactose are disaccharides (two sugar units). Starch/glycogen are polysaccharides; glucose, galactose, ribose and xylose are monosaccharides.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A biological community in its environment (a pond, ocean, forest or aquarium) is known as a/an
exp: An ecosystem is a biological community of organisms together with their physical (abiotic) environment, interacting as a unit.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which limits the number of trophic levels in a food chain?
options: decrease in the available energy at higher trophic levels
exp: Only about 10% of energy passes to the next trophic level (the rest is lost as heat/metabolism), so after a few levels too little energy remains to support more — limiting chain length.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which correctly describes the flow of energy and nutrients in an ecosystem?
options: Energy flow cyclic, nutrient flow unidirectional
Energy flow unidirectional, nutrient flow cyclic
exp: Energy flows one way (sun → producers → consumers, lost as heat) and cannot be reused, while nutrients are recycled through biogeochemical cycles.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is an end-to-end secure mobile ecosystem recently developed by the Indian Army?
exp: SAMBHAV (Secure Army Mobile Bharat Version) is the Indian Army's indigenous, end-to-end secure mobile communication ecosystem. (A defence/current-affairs item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which one is correct?
options: Guindy National Park is known for tiger reserve.
Namdapha National Park is meant for lion conservation.
Rann of Kutch is a Wild Ass Sanctuary.
exp: The Rann of Kutch (Gujarat) hosts the Indian Wild Ass Sanctuary. Namdapha is a tiger/biodiversity park (not lions), and the other pairings are wrong.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not a biosphere reserve of India?
exp: The Great Himalayan is a National Park (a World Heritage Site), not a biosphere reserve. Agasthyamalai, Nokrek and Great Nicobar are designated biosphere reserves.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Regarding the Gulf Stream, which statement is not correct?
options: It is similar to the Kuroshio current in the North Pacific.
It transports warm tropical water toward the polar region.
It is a major factor in weather along the east coast of the USA.
Its warm water sustains the coral reefs of the West Pacific coast.
exp: The Gulf Stream is an Atlantic current; it cannot affect coral reefs of the West Pacific coast — so statement d is false. (A geography item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which National Parks are declared World Heritage Sites by UNESCO?
exp: Keoladeo, Sundarbans and Kaziranga are UNESCO World Heritage Sites; Ranthambore is not. (A geography item.)
subs: 1. Keoladeo
2. Sundarbans
3. Kaziranga
4. Ranthambore.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Coral reefs are not found in which region?
exp: India's main coral reefs are in the Gulf of Mannar, Gulf of Kachchh, Lakshadweep and Andaman & Nicobar. The Gulf of Cambay, with heavy sediment and strong tides, has no coral reefs. (A geography item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: In 2020, which tiger reserve was declared a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve?
exp: Panna Tiger Reserve (Madhya Pradesh) was added to UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves in 2020. (A current-affairs item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which biosphere reserve comprises islands with estuaries, beaches, coral reefs, salt marshes and mangroves?
exp: The Gulf of Mannar reserve contains 21 islands plus coral reefs, seagrass beds, mangroves and salt marshes — the full mix described. (A geography item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: About Khijadiya Bird Sanctuary:
exp: Khijadiya was designated a Ramsar site (1, correct) but it is in Gujarat, not Uttar Pradesh, so statement 2 is wrong. (A current-affairs item.)
subs: 1. It was recently declared a Ramsar Site.
2. It is located in Uttar Pradesh.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Regarding Bhindawas, Sultanpur, Thol Lake and Wadhwana:
exp: All four are Ramsar sites (1) and important birding sites (3), but several are man-made/managed wetlands, so "all naturally formed" (2) is false. (A current-affairs item.)
subs: 1. All are Ramsar sites.
2. All are naturally formed wetlands.
3. All are birding sites.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which State/UT has the largest area under coral reefs in India?
exp: The Andaman & Nicobar Islands have by far the largest coral-reef area in India. (A geography item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The Ramsar Convention relates to which area?
exp: The Ramsar Convention (1971) is the intergovernmental treaty for the conservation and wise use of wetlands.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Cheetahs from Namibia were introduced in India to which National Park?
exp: Under Project Cheetah (2022), cheetahs from Namibia were reintroduced at Kuno National Park, Madhya Pradesh. (A current-affairs item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which pair is not correctly matched?
exp: The Arunachal Pradesh pairing (d) is the incorrect match. The other three sanctuary–state pairings are correct. (A geography item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which organisation publishes the worldwide list of endangered species?
exp: The IUCN maintains the Red List of Threatened Species, the global authority on conservation status.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not a thematic area of the National Mission on Sustainable Habitat?
options: Rural Planning, Green cover and Biodiversity
exp: The mission focuses on urban sustainability (energy/green buildings, mobility/air quality, waste, urban planning, water), so the "Rural Planning" theme is not part of it. (A governance item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which Ramsar wetland site is not situated in any Union Territory of India?
options: Point Calimere Wildlife and Bird Sanctuary
exp: Point Calimere is in Tamil Nadu (a State), whereas Hokera and Wular (J&K) and Tsomoriri (Ladakh) lie in Union Territories. (A geography item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: About Australia:
exp: The Great Barrier Reef lies in the Coral Sea off Queensland; the Coral Sea does not 'separate' it from the South Pacific, so statement 1 is wrong. The Great Dividing Range runs along eastern Australia, not from Melbourne to Perth, so statement 2 is wrong. Hence neither 1 nor 2.
subs: 1. The Coral Sea separates the Great Barrier Reef from the South Pacific.
2. The Great Dividing Range extends from Melbourne to Perth.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement about Nilgiri, Surat and Vagsheer is correct?
options: They are Tiger Reserves in Gujarat.
They are combatants commissioned by the Indian Navy.
They are Biodiversity parks maintained by the Indian Army.
They are Tiger Reserves maintained by the Indian Navy.
exp: INS Nilgiri and INS Surat are warships, and INS Vagsheer is a submarine — all commissioned by the Indian Navy. (A defence/current-affairs item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Consider the following statements:
options: Both true, II not the explanation
exp: Global warming is the rise in surface temperature (I), and it is caused by rising greenhouse gases (II) — so II correctly explains I.
subs: Statement I: Global warming signifies the rise in global surface temperature.
Statement II: An increase in greenhouse-gas concentration causes the rise in global surface temperature.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: One carbon credit is accepted as equivalent to
exp: One carbon credit = one tonne (1000 kg) of CO₂ (or equivalent greenhouse gas) reduced/avoided.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: About the GEF Grant Agreement (Aug 2017, World Bank, Ecosystems Service Improvement Project), which statement is not correct?
options: The project size is about USD 25 million.
It is financed entirely by the World Bank from its GEF Trust Fund.
The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change will implement it.
exp: The project duration was about 5 years, not 15 — so statement b is false. (A current-affairs item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: About the National Wildlife Action Plan (NWAP) 2017–2031:
exp: It is indeed the third NWAP (1) and the first to address climate change impacts on wildlife (2). It has five components, not ten, so statement 3 is wrong. (A governance item.)
subs: 1. It is the third NWAP.
2. It is the first time India recognised climate-change impact on wildlife.
3. It has ten components.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: About the National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change, which statement is not correct?
options: It helps meet the cost of adaptation measures at national and State levels.
It is a Central Sector Scheme.
The Indian Council of Agricultural Research is the national implementing entity.
It has been in force since 2015–16.
exp: The national implementing entity is NABARD, not ICAR — so statement c is false. (A governance item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The Janaki Ammal National Award on Taxonomy is administered by the
options: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
exp: The MoEFCC confers the Janaki Ammal Award (named after the eminent botanist) for taxonomy. (A governance item.)

stem: Which is the nodal agency in India for the United Nations Environment Programme?

stem: The National Disaster Management Authority functions under the Ministry of

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which UN organisation has been awarded the Nobel Prize twice?
exp: The UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) won the Nobel Peace Prize twice (1954 and 1981).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: About the Green Credit Initiative:

2. It promotes plantations on wasteland and river catchment areas.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: In June 2024, India signed an MoU with the USA to help Indian Railways achieve Mission Net Zero Carbon Emission by
exp: Indian Railways targets net-zero carbon emissions by 2030. (A current-affairs item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement is not correct?
options: SAGAR-SETU is a mobile app aimed at improving Ease of Doing Business.
Harit Sagar aims at achieving the Zero Carbon Emission goal.
Sagar Manthan is a mission to increase fish production.
Costa Serena is the first international cruise liner in India.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The Basel Convention aims at protecting human health and the environment against adverse effects of
exp: The Basel Convention controls the transboundary movement and disposal of hazardous wastes. (POPs → Stockholm Convention; mercury → Minamata Convention.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is the most important factor for the formation of smog?
options: Rapid fall in temperature with height
exp: A temperature inversion acts as a "lid" that traps pollutants near the ground, allowing them to accumulate and form smog. (A geography/environment item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement is not correct?
options: The market mechanism over-produces a good that generates a positive externality.
Cap-and-trade of pollution permits can achieve the social optimum.
The optimal subsidy for a positive-externality activity equals the gap between social and private benefit at the optimum.
The Tragedy of Commons is an example of a negative externality.
exp: A market actually under-produces goods with positive externalities (because private benefit is less than social benefit) — so statement a is false. (An economics item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), adopted by the UN in place of the MDGs, aim to achieve their 17 goals by
exp: The SDGs (Agenda 2030), adopted in 2015, set a target year of 2030.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not an exclusive right of a coastal nation over its Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ)?
options: Survey and exploitation of mineral resources
Exploitation of marine energy and organisms including fishing
Conservation and management of marine resources
Navigation of ships and laying of submarine cables
exp: Freedom of navigation and laying submarine cables are rights enjoyed by all states in the EEZ, not exclusive to the coastal nation (which has exclusive rights only over resource use). (A geography/law item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: About the National Green Tribunal, which statement is not correct?
options: It deals with expeditious disposal of environmental cases.
It may give relief and compensation for damages.
It is bound by the procedures of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
exp: The NGT is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure; it follows principles of natural justice — so statement d is false. (A governance item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which are considered the four pillars of human development?
exp: The UNDP's four pillars of human development are equity, productivity, empowerment and sustainability. (An economics item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which report defines Sustainable Development as "development that meets the needs of the present without compromising future generations"?
options: Agenda-21 of the Rio Earth Summit
exp: This classic definition comes from the Brundtland Report, "Our Common Future" (1987).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A UNGA resolution of 3 March 2021 decided to celebrate 2023 as the International Year of
exp: The UN declared 2023 the International Year of Millets (proposed by India) to promote these nutritious, climate-resilient crops. (A current-affairs item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is/are UN Sustainable Development Goals?
exp: All three are SDGs — Goal 8 (decent work), Goal 16 (peace, justice) and Goal 12 (responsible consumption).
subs: 1. Decent work and economic growth.
2. Peace, justice and strong institutions.
3. Responsible consumption and production.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which concepts are pillars of Human Development?
exp: The four pillars are equity, sustainability, productivity and empowerment — so among the listed items, 1, 2 and 3 qualify, while "security" (4) is not one of them. (An economics item.)
subs: 1. Equity
2. Sustainability
3. Productivity
4. Security.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: What does India's "Blue Growth" refer to?
options: Upgradation of the Indian Air Force
A long-term strategy to support sustainable growth in the marine and maritime sectors
exp: Blue Growth/Blue Economy is a strategy for sustainable use and development of ocean and maritime resources (fisheries, shipping, coastal tourism). (An economics item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: About the Mauryan State and forest people:
exp: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong — the State, not the forest people, claimed the monopoly over forest produce. So three statements are correct. (A history item.)
subs: 1. They were subjected to new political/economic dominance, changing the earlier policy of exclusion.
2. The State recognised forest produce as the sole monopoly of the forest people.
3. The State was concerned with forest conservation and prohibited burning of forests.
4. Forest people could serve as troops, spies and assassins. How many statements are correct?

subject: Science & Technology
stem: About the Marrakech Partnership:
exp: The Marrakech Partnership for Global Climate Action connects Parties (governments) with non-Party stakeholders (cities, businesses, investors) and aligns with the 2030 Agenda — statements 2 and 3 are clearly correct, and 1 captures its intergovernmental core. (Statements 1 and 2 overlap, so this item is worth checking against the official key.)
subs: 1. It is an intergovernmental partnership for global climate action.
2. It is not only intergovernmental but also a collaboration between governments and stakeholders like cities, businesses and investors.
3. It is guided by the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: India's Long-Term Low Emissions Development Strategy envisions:
exp: India's Long-Term Low Emissions Development Strategy (LT-LEDS) includes a just transition away from fossil fuels, increased use of biofuels, and climate-resilient urban development (statements 1, 2 and 3). Green bonds are not part of the listed framing - hence 1, 2 and 3.
subs: 1. a just, smooth, sustainable transition away from fossil fuels.
2. increased use of bio-fuels.
3. climate-resilient urban development.
4. financing of sustainable development through Green Bonds.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which was the focus of the Twelfth Five-Year Plan?
exp: The Twelfth Plan (2012–17) had the theme "Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth." (An economics item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not explained by Dalton's atomic theory?
options: Presence of different kinds of sub-atomic particles in an atom
exp: Dalton treated the atom as indivisible, so his theory could not account for sub-atomic particles (electrons, protons, neutrons). It did explain the laws of conservation of mass, constant composition and multiple proportions. (A chemistry item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement is not correct?
options: The Sun, Earth and Moon in a 180° straight line is called syzygy.
Syzygy conjunction causes a solar eclipse.
Syzygy opposition causes a lunar eclipse.
Syzygy conjunction occurs at the time of perihelion only.
exp: A syzygy (alignment) can occur at any point in the orbit, not only at perihelion — so statement d is false. The definitions of syzygy and of solar/lunar eclipses are correct. (Astronomy.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which planet was explored by NASA's Cassini Mission (ended September 2017)?
exp: Cassini studied Saturn, its rings and moons for 13 years, ending with a planned plunge into Saturn in 2017.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: "VENµS", the first environmental-research satellite, launched in August 2017, was launched by which country?
exp: VENµS (Vegetation and Environment monitoring on a New Micro-Satellite) was an Israeli–French satellite launched in August 2017. (A current-affairs item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement about Antrix Corporation Limited is correct?
options: Commercial arm of the Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion
Under the administrative control of the Department of Space
Under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Commercial arm of the Department of Science and Technology
exp: Antrix is the commercial/marketing arm of ISRO, under the Department of Space.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The Pragyan rover of the Chandrayaan-2 mission had how many wheels?
exp: The Pragyan rover had six wheels for moving on the lunar surface. (A current-affairs item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement about Anil Menon is correct?
options: An engineer who revolutionised organic farming
A diplomat in a UN agency
A physician selected by NASA to be an astronaut

subject: Science & Technology
stem: India's maiden human space mission (to be launched) is named

subject: Science & Technology
stem: About the James Webb Space Telescope:
exp: The JWST is the largest, most powerful space telescope, built by NASA in partnership with ESA and CSA. Both statements are correct.
subs: 1. It is the largest observatory ever launched into space.
2. It was developed by NASA with the European and Canadian Space Agencies.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is true for the James Webb Space Telescope (launched December 2021)?
options: It orbits the Sun, about 15 lakh km from Earth.
It orbits the Earth, about 15 lakh km away.
It is stationary nearly 10 lakh km from Earth.
It revolves around the Moon ~3.5 lakh km from Earth.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is the first commercial space station?
exp: Axiom Station is being built as the world's first commercial space station (initially attached to the ISS).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which were major ISRO missions of 2023?
exp: Chandrayaan-3 and Aditya-L1 were major ISRO missions of 2023 (statements 1 and 2). 'Liquid-fuel powered rockets' is a technology, not a mission, and 'solar-powered rockets' is not a valid mission category - so only 1 and 2 are correct.
subs: 1. Chandrayaan-3
2. Solar Mission Aditya-L1
3. Liquid-fuel powered rockets
4. Solar-powered rockets.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Mission Shakti of DRDO is related to which of the following?
options: Launch of multiple satellites using a single rocket
Use of a rocket to destroy an orbiting satellite
exp: Mission Shakti (2019) was India's anti-satellite (ASAT) test, destroying a satellite in low-Earth orbit. (A current-affairs item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: ISRO found a 178% increase in the size of the Ghepang Ghat Glacial Lake. It is located in
exp: The Ghepang Ghat glacial lake is in Lahaul-Spiti, Himachal Pradesh. (A current-affairs/geography item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which PSLV launched by ISRO in 2023 is not correctly matched with its mission?
exp: PSLV-C57 launched Aditya-L1, not DS-SAR (DS-SAR flew on PSLV-C55) — so this pairing is wrong. (A current-affairs item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement is not correct?

The name comes from the Brahmaputra and Moskva rivers.
Indian scientists integrated BrahMos with the Sukhoi-30 MKI.
DRDO is the manufacturer of the Sukhoi-30 MKI fighter.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The Government cleared production of 18 indigenous Dhanush artillery guns to be produced by

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement about the Missile Technology Control Regime is not correct?

Members prevent proliferation of missile/UAV technology capable of carrying >500 kg payload more than 300 km.
China applied to join but was not offered membership.
No country outside the membership follows the Regime rules.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The first Tejas squadron of the IAF consists of

subject: Science & Technology

India proposed the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism in 1996.
The CHOGM was held in 2016 at Malta.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement about the Wassenaar Arrangement is not correct?

stem: About India's military arsenal:

3. BrahMos missiles are built under an India–Russia joint venture.

subject: Science & Technology

subject: Science & Technology

subs: 1. Atmiya Sabha
2. Brahmo Samaj
3. Prarthana Samaj
4. Arya Samaj.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which Arab scientist is credited with naming the mathematical discipline of "algorithm"?

stem: The location of the ancient city of Taxila (Takshashila) was identified by

subject: Science & Technology
stem: About e-RUPI (prepaid digital vouchers):

subject: Science & Technology

subject: Science & Technology
stem: About widows in 18th-century India:

subs: 1. Raja Sawai Jai Singh of Amber promoted widow remarriage.

3. Raja Ram Mohan Roy opposed Sati.

subject: Science & Technology

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which language uses the symbolic representation of machine codes needed to program a particular processor?

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is not a logical operator?
exp: AND, OR and NOT are logical (Boolean) operators; division is an arithmetic operator.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: What are the purposes of deploying a firewall?
exp: A firewall inspects packets, blocks unauthorised access and suspicious activity (1, 2, 3). Interconnecting telephones (4) is unrelated.
subs: 1. Examine each packet arriving from the Internet.
2. Prevent unauthorised access.
3. Block suspicious activity.
4. Interconnect telephones.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is the largest source of electricity in India?
exp: Thermal (mainly coal-based) power plants generate the largest share of India's electricity. (An energy item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which ministry was recently formed under the Government of India?
options: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of Development of North-Eastern Region
exp: The Ministry of Cooperation was created in July 2021 ("Sahkar se Samriddhi"). (A current-affairs item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement about biogas is not correct?

It is a non-renewable source of energy.
It is formed by decomposition of cow dung in the absence of oxygen.
It burns without smoke and leaves no residue.
exp: Biogas is renewable (continuously produced from organic waste) — so statement b is false. It is mainly methane, formed by anaerobic decomposition, and burns cleanly.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Manikaran in Himachal Pradesh is known for
exp: Manikaran is famous for its hot springs, a site of geothermal energy. (A geography item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is an exhaustible but renewable natural resource?
exp: Usable freshwater can be depleted (exhaustible) yet is replenished through the water cycle (renewable). Solar energy is inexhaustible; soil/landscape form too slowly to be "renewable" in human terms.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: A spacecraft was launched, running exclusively on solar power, to study which target — being the farthest from the Sun to do so?
exp: NASA's Lucy mission to Jupiter's Trojan asteroids is the farthest solar-powered spacecraft from the Sun. (A current-affairs item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which does not influence ocean currents?

exp: The Sun and Moon's gravity drives tides, not ocean currents. Currents are driven by solar heating, prevailing winds and the Coriolis effect. (A geography item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: The Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope consists of

exp: RDSO (Lucknow) is the research and standards body of the Indian Railways.

subject: Science & Technology

exp: India's first dedicated OPD for transgender persons was inaugurated at Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital, New Delhi (confirmed by PIB) - option d.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which statement about India's surgical strike inside Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir is correct?

It was not given any name.
It was sanctioned by the United Nations.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Who first arrived in Africa as traders, eventually leading to European colonization?
exp: The Portuguese were the first Europeans to establish trading contacts along the African coast (15th century), opening the way to later colonization. (A history item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: About the Sanyasi and Faqir disturbances:

2. There were Shaivite Naga Sanyasis in armed bands.
3. Majnu Shah, leading bands from 1771, was a prominent leader.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Regarding environmental problems from plastics, which statement is correct?
options: They do not get released into water and food.
They have no biochemical synthesis activity.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which were objectives of the G20 Summit 2023 under India's presidency?

2. Accelerating progress on SDGs
3. Women-led development.

stem: Which statement about the Tashkent Agreement is correct?

An agreement between India and Pakistan.
An agreement that led to the formation of Bangladesh.
An agreement between India and Mongolia.

subject: Science & Technology

stem: In medieval India, indigo extraction improved greatly as a result of

mechanical crushing tools for indigo stems
use of gypsum and lime mortars to make indigo vats water-proof
slave labour for desilting indigo crucibles
exp: Lining the vats with gypsum/lime mortar made them water-tight, allowing controlled fermentation and better indigo yield. (A history item.)

A pattern of stars that may not be equidistant from the Earth
A pattern of planets in the sky

exp: From Hooke's law F = kx, k = F/x has units of newton per metre (N/m).

The fusion bomb dropped at Nagasaki
The first nuclear bomb tested by America
The first nuclear bomb tested by North Korea

subject: Science & Technology

Chandragupta II, Kumaragupta I, Skandagupta and Budhagupta issued silver coins.

exp: Gravitational force follows the inverse-square law (F ∝ 1/r²); doubling the distance reduces the force to 1/4.

Neutrons are located inside the atomic nuclei.
Neutrons revolve around the atomic nuclei.

subject: Science & Technology

It is absent at the Equator.
It deflects wind to the right in the southern hemisphere.
It deflects wind to the right in the northern hemisphere.

subject: Science & Technology

poor in both potash and phosphorus
rich in potash and poor in phosphorus

options: All wires have the same resistivity
exp: Resistivity is an intrinsic material property — it depends only on the material (copper) and temperature, not on length or cross-section. So all three have the same resistivity.

subject: Science & Technology

exp: Slaked lime [Ca(OH)₂] reacts with atmospheric CO₂ (A) to form calcium carbonate, CaCO₃ (B), which gives walls their hard, shiny white finish.

subject: Science & Technology

options: the net force acting on it
the total of all forces acting on it irrespective of direction
the force it exerts on the ground
exp: Strictly, weight is the gravitational force exerted by the Earth on the object (W = mg) — none of the options states this cleanly. Among the choices, the gravitational pull is intended; the option wording is imprecise, so this item should be checked against the official key.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which material is present in a guard tube (drying tube) used in the preparation of HCl gas?
exp: Anhydrous calcium chloride is a drying agent that absorbs moisture, keeping the HCl gas dry in the guard tube.

exp: These are soil orders in the USDA soil-taxonomy classification. (A geography item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which is a typical example of monopolistic competition?
exp: Monopolistic competition features many sellers offering differentiated (branded) products — the soap market (many brands) is the classic example. (An economics item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: What happens to the gravitational force between two objects if the mass of one is doubled and the distance is also doubled?
options: The force increases by a factor of 4
exp: F ∝ m/r². Doubling the mass multiplies F by 2; doubling the distance divides F by 4. Net effect: 2/4 = ½, so the force is halved.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which land surface has the highest albedo?
exp: Fresh snow reflects most incoming sunlight (highest albedo, ~80–90%), far more than rock, sand or vegetation. (A geography item.)

subject: Science & Technology

options: At least 30% of the planet protected by 2030
30% of cultivated area under organic farming by 2030
30% of the poor lifted out of poverty by 2030
exp: The "30x30" biodiversity goal (Kunming-Montreal framework) aims to protect at least 30% of land and oceans by 2030. (A current-affairs item.)

subject: Science & Technology

Desert, Tropical thorny, Moist deciduous, Mangrove
Moist deciduous, Tropical thorny, Mangrove, Desert
Desert, Tropical thorny, Mangrove, Moist deciduous
exp: Going from arid Bikaner (desert) eastward across the thorny scrub, into the wetter moist deciduous belt, and finally the coastal mangroves near Konark (Odisha). (A geography item.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which pair of metals are very good conductors of heat?
exp: Silver and copper are the two best metallic conductors of heat (and electricity). Lead and mercury are relatively poor conductors.

subject: Science & Technology

subject: Science & Technology

exp: Both Venus and Mars have atmospheres that are about 95–97% carbon dioxide. (Astronomy.)

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Which method is used to separate the constituents present in a compound?
exp: A compound can only be broken into its elements by chemical means such as electrolysis (an electrochemical method) — physical methods like distillation only separate mixtures.

subject: Science & Technology

subject: Science & Technology

Minimum potential energy at Q and S
Same potential energy at all positions

subject: Science & Technology

2. Venus has two moons.

subject: Science & Technology

Rise of pressure due to particulates
Rise of temperature due to particulates
Fall of temperature due to increased particulates

keep it in an AC room (~23 °C) with a fan at slow speed
keep it in a bowl of water at room temperature with a fan at full speed
keep it in a bowl of water at room temperature only
